item.title: Eight-Pole Narrow-Rail Coupler With Cross Section Modulated Cores and an SPQ Receiver for Stable-Output Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer
item.description: This work proposes an eight-pole narrow-rail coupler for dynamic wireless power transfer. An equivalent eight-pole field is generated by a specific winding arrangement, and a cross-sectional area compensation approach is proposed to suppress mutual inductance fluctuations and thereby reduce output power fluctuation. On the receiver side, a solenoid-planar quadraturecoil is proposed, where the two coils are not only naturally decoupled but also enable current sharing. Based on this dual-receiver structure, a design method for maximizing the equivalent coupling coefficient is further developed. Experimental results show that at a power level of 5 kW, with a transmitter rail core width of only 2 cm, the power fluctuation rate is 7.38%, the efficiency fluctuation rate is 0.67%, and the transmission efficiency reaches 93.03%. Moreover, current sharing is achieved at any position without the need for additional control.

item.title: Deep Vertical Integration With Embedded Gate Driver and Rogowski Coil Toward SiC Intelligent Power Module
item.description: To fertilize the ancillary functionality and power density of the silicon carbide (SiC) power module, the compact SiC intelligent power module (IPM) concept with built-in gate driver and Rogowski coil is proposed and realized with standard EasyPack packaging for industrial applicability in this letter. By exploiting the z-axis space of the packaging, the gate driver is inserted into the power module and co-designed with the bare die layout to minimize the gate driver loop and improve the transient switching behavior. Moreover, a nonintrusive Rogowski coil current sensor with a simplified passive integrator is developed and embedded into the compact SiC IPM to enable high-bandwidth short-circuit current detection and reliable protection. Comprehensive experiments with double-pulse test and short-circuit protection demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed SiC IPM concept. With the aid of deep integration in the z-axis space of the packaging, the proposed SiC IPM concept provides an effective solution for the high intelligence and high power density SiC converter applications.

item.title: A Fully Soft-Switched Primary Parallel Compensated IPT System for Entire Load and Coupling Variations in EV Applications
item.description: A current source inverter (CSI)-fed primary-parallel compensated inductive power transfer (IPT) system has great potential to achieve soft-switching at the turn-onand turn-offof CSI devices. This is because the voltage across the CSI devices follows a sinusoidal profile with natural zero crossings in every switching cycle. However, in the CSI-fed IPT system, the resonance depends on load and coupling ($k$) variations. Therefore, variation in load and $k$ leads to hard-switching of the CSI devices, and further results in short-circuiting of the primary parallel compensation capacitor, $C_{p}$. To prevent this, the conventional CSI-fed IPT system uses additional series diodes, auxiliary circuits, or additional control, which increase losses, cost, and complexity. This letter proposes a novel $C_{p}$ design that achieves zero-voltage switching at turn-on and at turn-offof all CSI switches. The proposed design achieves soft-switching under all possible load and $k$ variations, making it suitable for dynamic electric vehicle charging applications. All analysis findings are verified by experimental results from an 800-W lab prototype, achieving an efficiency of 97%.

item.title: Mechanical Parameter Design for Implantable BCI Wireless Charging Systems
item.description: Titanium enclosures of implantable brain– computer interfaces introduce severe eddy current loss (ECL) and thermal safety risks during wireless charging. This letter proposes a three-coil equivalent circuit model to decouple mechanical and electrical parameter effects, avoiding high-dimensional simulation-based optimization. Closed-form solutions are derived for the optimal current phase difference and minimum ECL. The design dimensionality is effectively reduced to simplify mechanical parameter optimization. Experimental results validate the model's high accuracy. The optimized prototype reduces the titanium-housing volume by 45%, restricts temperature rise within the ${\text{2}}\; ^\circ {\text{C}}$ safety limit, and maintains steady 700 mW output power.

item.title: Dynamic Current Imbalance Mechanism Analysis of Paralleled SiC MOSFETs Based on a Multibranch Parasitic Network Model Considering Common-Path Inductances
item.description: Dynamic current imbalance significantly degrades the electrothermal reliability of multibranch paralleled SiC mosfets, necessitating accurate mechanism analysis. Existing multibranch parasitic network models typically incorporate common-path parasitic inductances into branch parasitic inductances, which obscures the resulting interbranch current coupling and its impact on dynamic current imbalance. To address this issue, this article develops a multibranch parasitic network model in which common-path parasitic inductances are characterized separately from branch parasitic inductances. The proposed model reveals that common-path parasitic inductances govern the dynamic current distribution among branches through an intrinsic negative-feedback current-coupling mechanism. Specifically, in the subthreshold region, the initial dynamic current imbalance is mainly governed by the drive-source common-path parasitic inductance, whereas in the saturation region, the peak dynamic current imbalance is primarily governed by the power-source common-path parasitic inductance. PCB-level experiments validate the proposed model and mechanism analysis. Furthermore, to demonstrate the practical value of the proposed model, a stepwise optimization method based on the sensitivity ranking of parasitic inductances is proposed. Module-level experiments show that the dynamic current imbalance is reduced from 56.1% to 3.5%.

item.title: An Improved Signal Mixing Method Based on Tunnel Magnetoresistance-Rogowski Coil Sensors for SiC MOSFETs
item.description: Wide-band current sensors with DC capability are crucial for characterizing both steady state and high-frequency transients in switched-mode power electronics and digital control. Traditional hybrid sensors often suffer from complex circuitry, need for precise tuning, high component count, and elevated cost. This article presents an improved signal mixing method based on tunneling magnetoresistive (TMR) sensors and Rogowski coil sensors. By directly winding the TMR output leads into a Rogowski coil, which is the distinctive design of this work, the two signals are combined without additional complex circuitry. Using only one hybrid integrator, the proposed method achieves a bandwidth from DC to 54.9 MHz, significantly simplifying design and reducing cost. The sensor exhibits linear deviation within 2% and a resolution of 0.1 A at 5 MHz. Double-pulse tests using SiC mosfets further demonstrate its potential for switch transient testing of high-frequency power semiconductors.

item.title: Mechanical Power Sharing and Torsional Vibration Suppression Control for Dual Motor Drive System
item.description: To increase system power capacity and improve the reliability of industrial conveyor systems, a modularized dual-inverter direct-driven machine is developed to supply a common mechanical load. Communication-less control approach using speed/electromagnetic torque droop characteristic is widely used for mechanical load power sharing. However, the existing load sharing control considers only rigid drivetrain, which cannot reveal system torsional vibration behavior. In this article, it is found that the control targets of load sharing and torsional vibration suppression are strongly coupled. The speed droop coefficient will provide a certain damping ratio, while the active damping feedback gain will also affect the speed dynamic response. Systematic controller design methods are provided to achieve optimized power sharing, dynamic response, and torsional vibration suppression performance simultaneously. Another original finding is that active damping feedback gain can be set as zero or a negative value when the load to machine inertia ratio is larger than 16 to achieve critical damping. Finally, hardware-in-the-loop and experimental tests are done to verify the findings.

item.title: Robust Soft-Switching Inverter Design for Electric Motors With Significant Parasitic Capacitances
item.description: The ARCP) inverter stands out in the class of soft-switching inverters. With the increasing maturity of silicon carbide (SiC) devices, it has become feasible to develop high power ARCP inverters for drive applications. In an ARCP inverter, the resonant current supplied by the auxiliary circuit enables the soft-switching operation. However, parasitic capacitors from the electric motors to the system ground make a common-mode path, causing high-frequency ripples in the load current, which is usually in the range of several MHz. These high-frequency ripples in the load current affect the charging and discharging of resonant capacitors in the auxiliary circuit, leading to soft-switching failures. To address this issue, this article proposes design and optimization methods for the resonant circuit and resonant current. Achieving robust soft switching operation reduces voltage overshoot across SiC power devices and their current stresses, improving the robustness and reliability of the inverter and motor-drive system. Extensive experimentation of the ARCP inverter is carried out by authors and selected results are presented to quantify the influence of the motor parasitic capacitance. Compared with the conventional design approach, the proposed method reduces the residual turn-on voltage from more than 150 V to nearly 0 V and achieves successful soft-switching operation across all tested phase-current levels under both RL-replica and motor load. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method to achieve soft switching with the presence of substantial motor parasitics.

item.title: A Phase-Sequence Optimized Control Strategy of Harmonic Currents for Excitation Enhancement in Multiphase Brushless Wound-Field Synchronous Motor at Zero and Low Speeds
item.description: Multiphase brushless wound-field synchronous motors (MBWFSMs) enable excitation at zero and low speeds by injecting high-frequency harmonic currents to generate rotating harmonic magnetomotive forces. However, conventional excitation strategies typically apply phase-sequence principles inherited from three-phase systems without fully exploiting the inherent phase-control flexibility of multiphase high-frequency harmonic currents, thereby limiting field current enhancement. To address this issue, this article proposes a field current enhancement strategy based on phase-sequence optimized control of the multiphase high-frequency harmonic currents. First, an analytical harmonic coupling model of the MBWFSM is established, elucidating the mechanism by which high-frequency harmonic currents induce electromotive forces (EMFs) in rotor harmonic windings through air-gap field modulation, which are then rectified to supply the field winding. Second, the influence of high-frequency harmonic currents on the field current under different phase-sequence coefficients (P = 1, 2, …, 10) is investigated. Then, an optimized phase-sequence configuration is proposed to enhance the induced EMF in the rotor harmonic windings, thereby increasing the field current. Finally, experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, demonstrating that the optimized strategy significantly enhances the field current compared to the conventional phase-sequence control method.

item.title: Coordinated Multivariable Dithering Strategy for EMI Suppression in Wide-Range Resonant DC–DC Converters
item.description: With the advent of GaN devices, the operating frequency of power converters can be increased, particularly the high voltage resonant DC–DC converters. This negatively impacts the common-mode and differential-mode spectrum, necessitating an additional filtering requirement which defeats the purpose of high frequency operation to shrink passive component size. To tackle this specific problem, this article presents a coordinated multivariable dithering strategy for electromagnetic interference (EMI) suppression in wide-range resonant DC–DC converters. The proposed constraint-driven dithering control method effectively suppresses EMI by coordinating frequency modulation with timing control variables through gain-invariant mapping, ensuring enhanced system stability, voltage regulation, and compliance with stringent EMI standards. Its versatility is demonstrated in various operating modes, including DC transformer, buck, and boost modes. A detailed theoretical analysis is presented, supported by mathematical derivations and simulation results, to illustrate the dynamic interplay between frequency dithering and phase shift to control voltage gain. Experimental validation on a single-phase onboard charger hardware prototype confirms significant EMI attenuation, especially at the higher frequency end of the conducted EMI spectrum, while maintaining high efficiency and stable operation over a wide voltage range. These findings highlight the potential of the method for compact and efficient EMI management in electric vehicle charging and data-center applications.

item.title: Common-Mode Noise Optimization via Impedance-Balanced Design in Three-Phase Four-Wire Systems
item.description: Building on a path analysis of common-mode (CM) noise in three-phase four-wire on-board chargers (OBCs), this article proposes an impedance-balanced design that exploits the inherent parasitic inductance of the neutral (N) conductor. By connecting a compensation branch to the DC-bus midpoint, a Wheatstone-bridge-type CM path is formed and CM noise is suppressed. Small-signal insertion-loss measurements are first employed to rapidly. extract the N-line parasitic inductance, from which the initial compensation capacitance for bridge balance is calculated. The article further clarifies that the reduction of line-frequency leakage current originates from relocating the line-to-ground capacitive connection from the phase lines to the low-AC-potential DC-bus midpoint, whereas the broadband CM-noise suppression in 150 kHz–30 MHz originates from the bridge-balancing interaction that includes the N-line parasitic inductance. Moreover, subtle component parasitics—such as the power factor correction (PFC)-inductor equivalent parasitic capacitance and the X-capacitor equivalent series inductance—are shown to shift the bridge balance point, and degrade the filtering effect. To address this, a genetic algorithm searches in the frequency domain for the optimal compensation impedance that accounts for these parasitics and achieves improved broadband impedance matching. Additional controlled comparisons using the same compensation impedance at different mounting locations verify that the improvement is dominated by impedance balancing rather than by simply increasing shunt capacitance. Experiments on a loaded OBC and an auxiliary single-phase boost PFC prototype validate the approach. Compared with an equal-valued capacitor placed on the AC side, the proposed midpoint-connected optimized impedance provides an additional 5–30 dB reduction in the tested frequency ranges.

item.title: Framework of LSTM-Based Direction-Dependent Asymmetric Operator Model for B-H Prediction Under Transient Excitations
item.description: Modeling magnetic B-H hysteresis remains a significant challenge, particularly when addressing nonperiodic transient signals containing diverse frequency components. In modern power electronics, accurate transient B-H prediction is increasingly critical for thermal management, circuit protection, and high-frequency magnetic design. Motivated by the MagNet Challenge II, this article introduces a novel long short-term memory -based direction-dependent asymmetric operator framework for transient B-H modeling. By combining data-driven techniques with elementary operators, the framework offers a flexible spectrum of model configurations, enabling users to balance training cost, computational efficiency, and accuracy. Pareto-front optimization is employed to select suitable configurations, which are subsequently verified on the complete MagNet open-source datasets containing ten different magnetic materials. The proposed model demonstrates robust performance, achieving an average sequence root-mean-square error between 1.82% and 5.30%, and a weighted relative mean error for energy loss between 2.11% and 3.16% across all tested materials. Built upon this framework, the models are further evaluated under the five scenarios of MagNet Challenge II, which closely reflect practical concerns, and achieve the highest accuracy in both sequence and energy evaluations among all participating models.

item.title: Nonsequential Multiobjective Integrated Optimal Design of LLC Resonant Converters Based on Interlinking Variables
item.description: Recent advances in LLC resonant converters have intensified the demand for effective multiobjective optimization techniques to achieve higher efficiency, increased power density, and improved thermal stability. This article presents an interlinking-variable-based nonsequential integrated multiobjective optimization framework tailored for LLC resonant converters. Unlike conventional sequential optimization approaches that treat the magnetizing inductance and the resonant inductance as fixed targets imposed between separate design stages, the proposed method redefines these values as explicit functions of the magnetic design variables, removing the equality constraints inherent in the sequential structure and unifying all circuit-level and magnetic-level design variables within a single optimization process. The interlinking relationships are evaluated through a hybrid analysis model combining time-domain circuit analysis with an ANN-based magnetic surrogate. Hardware prototypes designed by the proposed and conventional sequential methods are fabricated and experimentally compared. The proposed method improves the converter efficiency by 1.3%, reduces the total component volume by 9.0%, and decreases the total computation time by 56% compared with the conventional sequential design.

item.title: Leakage Inductance Calculation Method of High-Frequency Transformer Based on Monte Carlo Method and the Research on Transverse Magnetic Field Distribution Characteristics
item.description: Leakage inductance, a critical parameter in high-frequency transformers (HFTs), plays a significant role in the power transmission characteristics of power electronic transformers. In design, Litz wire is frequently employed to suppress the high-frequency eddy current effect, the complex stranded structure of Litz wire presents challenges in accurately calculating leakage inductance, which increased calculation costs and reduced efficiency. Therefore, this article utilizes the image method to construct an analytical expression for the magnetic field and calculates the leakage magnetic energy of the winding window using the Monte Carlo method, according to the difference in the distribution of magnetic field in different areas of the winding window, accurate capture of nonuniform magnetic field distribution can be achieved by dynamically adjusting the sampling density. A method of calculating the transverse magnetic field component of the conductor is proposed to construct the coupling model that considers the combined effect of internal and external magnetic fields, it realizes the accurate calculation of magnetic field distribution in the conductor area. Establish a precise calculation model for wide-frequency leakage inductance in two-dimensional polar coordinates, taking into account the eddy current and winding edge effect. Finally, four HFTs with different Litz wires are designed and built, the results show that the global average relative errors of the proposed method are 1.297%, 2.248%, 0.655% and 2.609%, respectively, which verify the accuracy of the described method.

item.title: A Scalable Flying-Capacitor Multilevel Drain Supply Modulator for Envelope Tracking Applications
item.description: A drain supply modulator based on the flying-capacitor multilevel (FCML) architecture is proposed for radio-frequency power amplifiers (RFPA) used in envelope-tracking transmitter systems. Operating from a single DC supply voltage, the FCML-based multilevel drain supply modulator (FCML-DSM) provides a multilevel drain voltage to the RFPA, to increase its efficiency while transmitting modulated signals with high peak-to-average power ratios. A four-level GaN-based prototype of the FCML-DSM is presented, with an output voltage range up to $\text{30} \,{\text{V}}$ and switching rates up to $\text{25} \,{\text{MHz}}$. The FCML-DSM employs a finite-state-machine controller to actively balance the flying-capacitor voltages and simultaneously control the output voltage level as required by the RFPA. An envelope-tracking test bench is implemented by connecting the supply modulator to a discrete $\text{10} \,{\text{W}}$ RFPA. Experimental results show that the FCML-DSM operates with greater than 95% efficiency while tracking three different test signals, with signal bandwidths up to $\text{20} \,{\text{MHz}}$. An improvement in overall transmitter efficiency is observed for each test signal. For a multitone $\text{20} \,{\text{MHz}}$ input signal, the transmitter efficiency increases from 31.3% with a constant supply voltage to 37.2% when the proposed multilevel drain supply modulation is applied.

item.title: Unified Analytical Framework With Inherent Feedback Model for (N−1)CNL Hybrid Converters Toward Fast Self-Balancing Dynamic Design
item.description: This article proposes a unified analytical framework to elucidate the self-balancing behavior of switched-capacitor hybrid converters, guiding the topology parameter optimization toward fast and stable self-balancing dynamics. The proposed general analyses are carried out from different perspectives and broadly applicable to different multiphase topologies featuring N–1 flying capacitors and N inductors. Distinct from existing analyses, first, the uniqueness criteria for steady-state current and voltage solutions are derived to identify the self-balancing capability of various hybrid topologies, and the impacts of duty cycle and parasitic resistance mismatches among phases are analyzed. Furthermore, a standard dynamic equation for transient balancing errors is derived, revealing the coupled-damped oscillation mechanism of the self-balancing under N-phase configuration. Finally, an inherent feedback model is established, providing a quantitative tool to optimize the self-balancing speed and stability. With this model, a topology parameter optimization method is developed to achieve fast and stable self-balancing. The proposed analysis and optimization are experimentally verified with a phase-reconfigurable prototype, where improved self-balancing dynamic performance is achieved through the topology parameter optimization.

item.title: High-Speed Synchronous Transmission Technology for Three-Phase Three-Channel Wireless Power and Reverse Signal
item.description: To overcome the limitations of existing single-phase simultaneous wireless power and reverse signal transmission (SWPRST) systems, including single-channel transmission, low spectral utilization, and limited data rate, this article proposes a three-phase SWPRST technique. By integrating three high-frequency signal injection circuits at the secondary side and three signal extraction and demodulation circuits at the primary side, synchronous transmission of power and high-speed reverse signals is achieved. The system configuration and operating principles are analyzed, and power and signal transmission channel models are established to evaluate power-channel crosstalk and adjacent-phase signal interference. Based on signal transmission gain and crosstalk characteristics, channel capacity is investigated, followed by parameter design and optimization under given constraints. An experimental platform is built to verify the proposed method. Results show that the system enables synchronous three-phase wireless power and reverse signal transmission, achieving 400 kbps per channel and a total transmission rate of 1.2 Mbps, with high efficiency, low power–signal crosstalk, and strong signal transmission performance.

item.title: An Interleaved-Fibonacci Always-Dual-Path Buck Converter With Large Voltage Conversion Ratio and Reduced Inductor Current
item.description: This article presents a 48-V-input, 3-V-to-5-V-output interleaved-Fibonacci always-dual-path buck converter, a hybrid topology that incorporates an interleaved Fibonacci switched-capacitor (SC) network and an always-dual-path structure. Among classical SC topologies, the interleaved Fibonacci SC topology achieves a large voltage conversion ratio with the fewest capacitors and offer a better tradeoff between slow- and fast-switching-limit output resistances. Compared with the conventional Fibonacci SC topology, it employs an improved switch strategy with distributed current and reduced voltage swing, resulting in superior fast-switching-limit performance. Moreover, the always-dual-path structure reduces the inductor current by 37.5%–62.5%, significantly reducing inductor DC resistance loss and mitigating the reliance on a bulky inductor. A hardware prototype was designed and built to validate the proposed converter. The prototype was tested with a maximum output power of 160 W, and achieves a peak efficiency of 95.5% for 48-V-to-5-V operation, as well as a power density of up to 953 W/in3 by box volume.

item.title: An Alternating Heating Power Cycling Test Method Mitigating Overly Conservative Lifetime Estimates of Power Electronics
item.description: Power cycling test (PCT) is the primary method for evaluating the packaging reliability of power electronics. However, conventional DC PCT neglects the alternating heating effect of insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) and its antiparallel diode, thus imposes excessive thermal stress, leading to overly conservative lifetime estimations. Although AC PCT methods can better emulate actual operating conditions, they are constrained by complex circuit topologies and reduced accuracy in junction temperature measurement. Moreover, existing studies have shown that AC PCT does not differ from DC PCT in terms of failure modes and lifetime. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes a novel alternating power cycling test (Alter-PCT) method that takes the alternating heating effect into account. This proposed method preserves the simplicity of test circuit and the accuracy of junction temperature monitoring. Comparative PCT were performed on 1200 V/25 A IGBT modules using DC PCT (as the benchmark) and Alter-PCT. Test results demonstrate that Alter-PCT significantly extends lifetime, and further, the failure analysis reveals that Alter-PCT markedly reduces the aging rates of both bond wires and solder layer.

item.title: A Thermal Modeling Method for Power Capacitors Under Long Timescale Dynamic Operation Profiles
item.description: This article proposes a thermal modeling method for film capacitors, which is applicable for high-power converters with long timescale dynamic operation profiles, such as traction and wind power systems. The proposed frequency domain modeling analyzes the effects of power loss and ambient temperature comprehensively in realistic mission profiles. Furthermore, the transfer function is discretized to concurrently obtain the iterative model with temperature rise by the influence of power loss and ambient temperature. This method has two advantages, as follows: First, discrete realistic operating profiles, including power loss and ambient temperature at different sampling times, can be conveniently introduced into the thermal model simultaneously. Second, the effect of temperature-dependent equivalent series resistance and thermal resistance can be further considered in discrete frequency domain modeling. The full power experiments for capacitor stress testing demonstrate the reasonableness and accuracy of the proposed method in hotspot temperature and lifetime expectancy calculations.

item.title: Asynchronous Stacking Architecture Decoupling Holding and Trigger Voltages for High-Voltage ICs ESD Protections
item.description: This article presents a novel asynchronously triggered stacking silicon-controlled rectifier (ATS-SCR) architecture for on-chip electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection in high-voltage integrated circuits. Fabricated in a 0.18- μm bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process, the proposed design integrates a low-trigger-current SCR (LISCR) and a high-trigger-current SCR (HISCR) with deliberately differentiated characteristics. Unlike conventional methods that stack two identical SCRs in series and thereby double both the trigger voltage (Vtr) and holding voltage (Vh), this asynchronous architecture effectively decouples the inherent tradeoff between these parameters. Measurement results demonstrate that the ATS-SCR achieves a high Vh to provide a robust safety margin against latch-up while maintaining a relatively low Vtr and a minimal ΔVdrift, defined as the difference between Vtr and the breakdown voltage, and thereby ensuring superior ESD protection capability. The working principle, validated through transmission line pulse testing, reveals a two-stage snap-back behavior governed by the sequential triggering of the LISCR and HISCR. This design provides a flexible and effective solution for improving the reliability of high-voltage systems, such as power management and automotive electronics.

item.title: Domain Generalization-Guided Power Converter Open-Circuit Fault Diagnosis: A Dynamic Decision Boundary Adaptation Strategy
item.description: Power converter fault diagnosis faces significant challenges from domain shift in industrial applications with varying operating conditions. Existing approaches struggle to capture dynamic spatio-temporal dependencies in multivariate current signals. This article proposes a domain generalization approach that integrates dynamic graph topology learning and adaptive decision boundary optimization. A dynamic graph convolutional layer with scaled dot-product self-attention is designed to adaptively infer topological connections, which extract high-order spatio-temporal features from power converter current signals. A dynamic decision boundary adjustment strategy introduces class-aware angular margins based on statistical distribution modeling with location-scale modified Student's $t$-distribution. This mechanism calculates safety margins dynamically according to interclass statistical distances, enabling robust classification without target domain samples. Experimental validation on a physical platform covering 21 fault types demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves 95.93 $\pm$ 1.14% average accuracy under cross-voltage operating conditions. The results indicate that the synergistic combination of dynamic graph modeling and adaptive boundary adjustment effectively mitigates distribution shift, providing a reliable solution for cross-domain insulated gate bipolar transistor fault diagnosis.

item.title: A Noninvasive Bond Wire Aging Monitoring Method Based on Combined Magnetic Flux Density
item.description: Bond wire aging monitoring is essential for assessing the health status of power devices in power converters. However, existing approaches typically require electrical connection to the converter and are susceptible to variations in the load current. To address these issues, this article proposes a noninvasive bond wire aging monitoring method based on the combined magnetic flux density (MFD). First, the MFD characteristics generated by multiple bond wires are thoroughly analyzed, and a new health indicator extracted from the combined MFD is developed, which is sensitive to different aging modes while being independent of temperature and load current. Furthermore, by integrating the minimum interclass distance and between-class variance, an evaluation system is constructed to determine the optimal sensor position with a minimal number of sensors. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is validated through comprehensive investigations, including theoretical analysis, finite-element simulations, and experimental verifications.

item.title: A Compact Piezoelectric Energy Harvester With Multi-Input ReL-SSHI Interface and Extensible MPPT Technique
item.description: This article presents a compact piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH) that utilizes a multi-input rectifier-less synchronized switch harvesting on inductor (ReL-SSHI) interface, along with an extensible maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique. The proposed interface allows the inductor current to maintain a unidirectional flow, addressing the charge neutralization issue. A novel extensible MPPT circuit based on the fractional average voltage method is proposed to monitor the vibration states of multiple piezoelectric transducers (PZTs). Both the ReL-SSHI interface and the MPPT circuits are designed to be compact, relying solely on self-powered passive components. This eliminates the need for active components such as comparators and logic units. Consequently, the proposed PEH operates without an external power source and significantly reduces overall power consumption. On average, each additional PZT requires only nine components for energy harvesting and five components for the MPPT. The ReL-SSHI interface circuit is capable of achieving a 4.2 times power improvement compared to the standard energy harvesting circuit, while the maximum MPPT efficiency reaches 99%.

item.title: Analysis and Mitigation of Grid Current Distortion in Single-Stage DAB AC–DC Converters With Minimum Peak Current
item.description: Power feedforward control is utilized in single-stage dual-active-bridge (DAB) AC–DC converters for natural power factor correction. However, this approach renders the grid current highly dependent on the modulation strategy and susceptible to practical circuit nonlinearities, which result in a mismatch between the actual and modeled power. In this article, the optimal operating modes to minimize peak current are first analyzed and the grid current constraints based on the conventional piecewise-linear model are derived to achieve the unity power factor. The continuity and sinusoidal purity of the grid current are then evaluated in terms of mode transitions and absolute power deviations. To address distortion issues, a charge-equivalent linearized commutation model is proposed. The proposed model achieves real-time equivalent linearization of the nonlinear commutation process during the dead time considering the magnetizing current. Based on the commutation model, the instantaneous power for single-stage DAB AC–DC converters is accurately determined. Furthermore, an automatic mode selection strategy and the computational flow are developed to mitigate grid current distortion. Finally, a 1-kW laboratory prototype with a 40-VDC output is constructed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

item.title: Grid-Forming Control With Self-Sustained Inertia and Transient Stability Enhancement for Type-IV Wind Turbines
item.description: Grid-forming (GFM) wind turbines represent a promising solution for integrating wind power into power systems due to their inherent grid-supporting capabilities. However, existing studies on the transient stability of GFM wind turbines remain incomplete. In particular, the impact of machine-side and DC-link voltage dynamics on grid-side transient stability is often overlooked. Furthermore, the enhancement of transient stability in GFM wind turbines considering their multitime-scale characteristics, has received limited attention. In this article, a Lyapunov-based energy function is derived that fully accounts for the dynamics of machine-side and DC-link voltage. Then, based on the extended invariance principle, the influence of system dynamic parameters on the transient stability of GFM wind turbines is revealed. An enhancement control strategy is proposed that leverages the fast response of the DC-link capacitor and the rotor's kinetic energy to actively absorb the power imbalances between the grid-side and machine-side during transients, effectively expanding the transient stability boundary and increasing the equivalent inertia. Both the theoretical analysis and the proposed strategy are verified through experiments.

item.title: A Cascaded Hybrid-Order ESO-Based ADRC for Voltage Regulation in Wave Energy DC Integration
item.description: As a renewable energy in the ocean, wave energy (WE) is converted into electrical energy, then integrated into a DC integration. However, the control strategy of PMSGs, and the topology and interaction among rectifiers would lead to fluctuation and bias of DC voltage. The DC-bus voltage regulation is essential for stable operation of WE-DC integration. In this article, a cascaded hybrid-order extended state observer (CHESO)-based active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) strategy is proposed for DC voltage support and disturbance suppression. First, the isolated WE-DC integration is modeled, and the disturbances in voltage are analyzed. Then, the proposed CHESO is constructed by a first-order augmented extended state observer (ESO) and a high-order augmented ESO in cascaded form to track DC voltage disturbance accurately, and the cascaded high-order augmented ESO compensates for the observation error. Furthermore, a single-loop DC voltage control structure based on CHESO-ADRC is proposed to simplify the original dual-loop control structure. Moreover, the CHESO and control law are designed independently. Compared with the dual-loop PI control strategy and original ADRC strategies, the CHESO-ADRC can track the DC voltage more quickly and accurately, and suppress voltage ripples with a better dynamic performance. Finally, the DC-bus voltage support and disturbance suppression of the proposed ADRC are verified.

item.title: Robust Power Flow Inverse Model Predictive Control for Multiactive Bridge Converters
item.description: This article presents a robust power flow control technique for multiactive bridge (MAB) converters that effectively deal with the system's nonlinear dynamics and associated uncertainties. The proposed methodology is based on inverse model predictive control (IMPC), which determines the optimal phase shift between bridges while effectively mitigating the coupling effects and nonlinear interactions in the MAB converters. Unlike conventional model predictive control (MPC), the IMPC approach avoids evaluating multiple phase-shift combinations, which substantially reduces computational complexity. Furthermore, the proposed control is designed to be robust against parametric uncertainties through feedback and correction loops, which represents a solution for a key challenge in the operation of highly nonlinear power converters. The proposed approach is experimentally implemented and validated on a lab-scale three-port MAB converter prototype. In addition, a comparative evaluation between the proposed IMPC and conventional MPC controllers is presented. The results show that IMPC delivers improved tracking accuracy over a wide range of operating conditions and uncertainties, while significantly reducing computational burden.

item.title: Grid Current Distortion Suppression of Single-Stage Dual-PV-Port DAB Microinverters via Synergetic Closed-Loop Control
item.description: The single-stage dual-photovoltaic (PV)-port dual-active-bridge (DAB) microinverter has emerged as a promising solution for residential PV systems, featuring reduced power conversion stages, wide soft-switching range, and high power density. However, port-to-port power coupling and pronounced dead-time effects are inherently introduced by its multiport architecture, leading to grid current quality degradation. Existing literature lacks a comprehensive analysis of these distortion mechanisms and effective suppression methodologies under asymmetric loading conditions. To address these challenges, a synergetic grid current closed-loop control scheme tailored for the single-stage dual-PV-port DAB microinverter is proposed. The operating principles enabling independent maximum power point tracking for each PV port are elucidated. Subsequently, the mechanism of grid current distortion induced by the interplay between dead-time effects and port coupling is revealed. A mode-wise gain compensation strategy is then proposed and integrated with zero-voltage-switching guaranteed port-decoupled modulation. Unlike conventional fixed dead-zone compensation, the proposed framework effectively suppresses current distortion, desensitizes parameter variations and enhances dynamic response without additional hardware. Finally, the theoretical analysis and the feasibility of the proposed strategy are validated through experimental results on a 1.2 kW prototype interfacing dual PV panels with a single-phase utility grid.

item.title: Closed-Loop Common Mode Current Mitigation for Transformerless Current-Source Soft Open Points
item.description: Compared to voltage-source converters (VSCs), current-source converters (CSCs) are characterized by simple topology, inherent DC short-circuit limitation, and high-quality input-output waveforms. However, the mechanism of common-mode currents (CMCs) generation in CSCs differs from that in VSCs, making the mitigation of CMCs in transformerless current-source soft open points (CS-SOPs) more challenging. To address this issue, a closed-loop approach based on optimal vector approximation space vector modulation (SVM) strategy is proposed. First, a common-mode equivalent circuit is established to derive the relationship between the CMC and common mode voltage (CMV). Then, an optimal vector approximation SVM is proposed, which achieves average CMV direct regulation through the optimal selection of zero vectors during each sampling period. Furthermore, the method effectively mitigates CMCs through a closed-loop control. Moreover, power loss analysis of the CS-SOP confirms that the proposed strategy incurs negligible additional losses and maintains high efficiency, ensuring its practical viability. Finally, experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

item.title: Hybrid Digital Twin-Based Health Monitoring and Parameter Estimation of Grid-Tied PV Systems
item.description: Predictive maintenance and real-time supervision in power electronic systems are now made possible in large part by digital twin technology. The hybrid digital twin (HDT)-based health degradation assessment approach for a grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system using a three-phase, four-leg inverter is presented in this article. The proposed HDT combines a physics-based Gauss–Legendre implicit Runge–Kutta (IRK) core with a data-driven long short-term memory (LSTM) network featuring a hybrid physics-data activation function. An LSTM refines latent-state estimates, including inductor currents and filter capacitor voltages, while the IRK solver enforces the system’s physical dynamics to reconstruct measurable quantities, such as grid currents and DC-link voltage. In order to ensure interpretability, adaptability, and data efficiency, an end-to-end training framework optimizes both physical parameters and neural weights. An HDT achieves a mean waveform correlation ($R^{2}$) of 0.981 across all signals and correctly identifies 46 system parameters with an average mean absolute error of 1.27%. System characteristics, such as generated and loss power, converter efficiency, DC-link voltage ripple, and grid current total harmonic distortion are used to evaluate the health assessment of important devices, such as the converter switch, DC-link capacitor, and interface inductor. A strong generalization is shown under a range of degradation levels. Submillisecond latency, high waveform fidelity, and robust degradation tracking are confirmed by experimental validation using an OPAL-RT (OP4512) platform and an NI sbRIO-9636 field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-controlled prototype, establishing the HDT as a physics-consistent framework for PV system diagnostics and monitoring.

item.title: Regulation of Multiharmonic Components for Nine-Phase Open-End Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
item.description: The nine-phase open-end winding (OW) permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) integrates the advantages of multiphase and OW topologies, making it an alternative solution for high-power propulsions. However, there is still a lack of efficient modulation methods for multiple ($\mathbf{\geq}$3) decoupling subspaces to address the multiharmonic current issue in this system. In this article, the advantages of model predictive control in handling multiobjectives and the virtual voltage vector (VVV) technique are utilized to achieve the active regulation of the fundamental, third-, fifth-, and seventh-order components. Unlike existing harmonic suppression strategies in multiphase AC machine drives, this study designs four sets of decoupled VVV to achieve the independent predictive control in four subspaces. Moreover, a multisubspace weight optimization algorithm is proposed to address the loss of harmonic control capability under voltage constraints. The proposed strategy is simple and easy to implement on industrial control platforms. Finally, experimental results validated the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, including a cost-performance comparison of controlling various harmonic components and selecting different constraint modes.

item.title: LLC Resonant Converter With Dual-Mode Reconfigurable Control and Three-Bridge Rectifier for a 50 kW Fast EV Charging Module
item.description: The LLC resonant converter is widely used for electric vehicle (EV) fast chargers due to its high efficiency via zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero current switching (ZCS). However, as the charging voltage range expands (250–1000 V), the LLC converter requires an excessively wide frequency variation, which degrades performance. To narrow this frequency range, conventional methods often incorporate bidirectional switches on the secondary side. However, such approaches inevitably lead to increased hardware complexity, higher implementation costs, and additional conduction losses. In this article, a novel LLC topology featuring two primary full-bridges and a three-bridge rectifier is proposed to achieve a wide output range with a simplified structure. By employing dual-mode reconfigurable control, the proposed converter maintains high efficiency across 250–1000 V using conventional PFM, without the need for additional bidirectional switches. A 50 kW prototype was developed, achieving a peak efficiency of 98.30% and maintaining over 97.16% across all conditions, validating the proposed design for high-power fast charging.

item.title: Maximum Efficiency Point Tracking Technology for Dual-Bridge Series Resonant Converter
item.description: Typically, the efficiency of a power electronic converter follows a parabolic trend, rising initially and then decreasing as the load current increases. To enhance efficiency in the ascending segment (left of the peak) of the quasi-parabolic efficiency curve, this article proposes a maximum efficiency point tracking (MEPT) technology that elevates the converter’s efficiency within this ascending segment to the maximum-efficiency point. The proposed MEPT technique is investigated using a dual-bridge series resonant converter (DBSRC) under extended-phase-shift and variable-frequency control as a representative case. By combining pulse skipping modulation with optimal trajectory control, the operating current during the pulse-retained cycles is regulated to match the load current corresponding to the maximum-efficiency point. As a result, the converter can operate equivalently at the maximum-efficiency point. In addition, the internal phase-shift angle, external phase-shift angle, and switching frequency remain fixed when the load current varies. Output regulation is achieved solely by adjusting the pulse-skipped ratio. This feature significantly reduces the control complexity compared with conventional multi-degree-of-freedom control schemes. Finally, a DBSRC prototype with input voltage range of 360–560 V and output voltage of 36.5 V is built to validate the proposed MEPT technology and the theoretical analysis.

item.title: SARSA-Based Smart Coordinated Strategy for Enhancing PV Array Performance Under Dynamic Shading Conditions
item.description: The performance of the photovoltaic (PV) array may deteriorate significantly under the partial shading condition (PSC). To reduce these harmful effects, this work introduces a new Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled state-action-reward-state-action (I-SARSA) algorithm that alters the interconnection of traditional total-cross-tied (TCT) PV arrays. The proposed algorithm runs by selecting the random reconfiguring matrix obtained using the IoT platform, following the existing epsilon-greedy policy, and updates its assigned location of PV modules in the form of Q-values. The developed I-SARSA algorithm uses a message queuing telemetry transport (MQTT) communication protocol that enables communication with PV modules and users while PSCs. Subsequently, the redistribution of the shaded PV module takes place dynamically, thereby minimizing mismatch losses and enhancing the global peak. Further, the performance parameters such as mismatch power loss (MPL), fill factor (FF), percentage power loss (%PL), and power enhancement are evaluated for the proposed and various existing approaches of dynamic PV array reconfiguration. The obtained results establish a substantial enhancement across all parameters, with up to 579 W reduced MPL compared to the conventional TCT and a %PL reduction up to 13.467%, hence proving to be a more competent sustainable energy solution. Moreover, the associated parameters of the PV arrays are monitored using the IoT platform. Furthermore, a hardware prototype has also been developed with an ATMEGA 25 board containing ESP 8266 and ICs 74LS138 to evaluate the performance measures of the proposed approach, where the results are found satisfactory.

item.title: A Dual-Slope Adaptive Feedback Strategy for Dynamic Voltage Balancing of Series-Connected SiC MOSFETs
item.description: Silicon carbide metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (SiC MOSFETs) can enhance the voltage withstand capability when operated in series. However, dynamic voltage imbalance caused by mismatches in parasitic parameters of devices or circuits is an inherent issue in series operation, which significantly degrades the service life of series-connected devices. Existing active schemes suffer from either a long voltage balancing period or a significant degradation of the inherent fast switching speed of SiC MOSFETs. In contrast, existing passive schemes are plagued by either considerable energy loss introduction or complex structures that are difficult to implement. To address these issues, this article proposes a novel passive voltage balancing strategy for dual-slope drain-source voltage (vds) of SiC MOSFETs. By employing simple components to enforce equal vds slew rates and controlling the circuit’s operation time, the proposed scheme minimizes the impact on switching speed as much as possible while achieving effective voltage balancing. Comparisons with the conventional gate drive (CGD) through experiments and with the existing best active scheme have verified that the proposed method can effectively achieve dual-slope vds driving and significantly reduce the impact of the voltage balancing circuit on switching speed (restricting the turn-off time to ∼120 ns compared to the ∼80 ns baseline, substantially outperforming the ∼300 ns required by the benchmark active scheme).

item.title: Efficiency Optimization Strategy for Single-Stage Resonant DAB Microinverter Based on Phase Shift Angle Decoupling Control
item.description: To reduce the turn-off loss of the single-stage resonant dual-active-bridge (SSRDAB) microinverter, this article proposes an efficiency optimization strategy based on phase shift angle decoupling control. By reconstructing the time-domain mathematic model, decoupled regulation of internal and external phase shift angles and switching frequency is achieved. On this basis, operating trajectories of the phase shift angles and switching frequency are designed to ensure zero-current turn-off of the secondary side switch. Furthermore, the key parameter of the proposed strategy is optimized by jointly considering soft-switching performance, reverse power suppression, and rms current minimization, enabling global efficiency optimization. Consequently, the turn-off loss of the SSRDAB converter is effectively reduced, while the coupled control variables and modeling complexity associated with zero-current turn-off operation are mitigated. As a result, high efficiency is achieved over a wide operating range. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated on a 300 W experimental prototype.

item.title: Inductance Identification Method for Dual Active Bridge Converters Considering Sampling Noise Over the Full Power Range
item.description: The dual active bridge (DAB) converter is widely used in energy storage systems (ESS) due to its bidirectional power flow capability and high efficiency. Extensive studies on advanced modulation and control strategies have been conducted to enhance the performance of DAB converters. However, these methods strongly rely on accurate inductance parameters. Existing parameter identification methods exhibit limited capability in suppressing sampling noise, making it difficult to achieve accurate identification over the entire power range. To address this issue, this article proposes a Sage-Husa inductance parameter identification method. First, the measurement noise variance is approximately estimated using a small number of samples, enabling the evaluation of sampling noise levels under different operating conditions. Then, the process noise variance is adaptively updated based on the variance of the prior error, thereby achieving accurate inductance identification over the full power range. In addition, considering the insufficient accuracy and operational complexity of conventional LCR meter, an inductance measurement method is proposed to provide a reliable reference for the identification results. Finally, to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a 200 W DAB converter prototype is built, and full power range inductance identification is implemented under an advanced extended dual-side asymmetric phase-shift modulation (EDAPSM) scheme. Experimental results verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

item.title: An Expert Trajectory Guided Online Energy Management Strategy for Aviation Fuel Cell Hybrid Power System
item.description: To meet the higher power output and real-time control requirements of aviation fuel cell hybrid power system, an online energy management strategy (EMS) for multienergy sources becomes essential. A reinforcement learning (RL) based online EMS is proposed in the article, which integrates expert trajectory guidance with autonomous exploration mechanism. During the offline phase, the strategy mimics power allocation actions based on trajectories generated by the dimension-reduction dynamic programming (DRDP) strategy. Subsequently, the trained agent is deployed online for performance validation. Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test results demonstrate that compared with demo-guided TD3 and demo-guided SAC, the proposed strategy can effectively reduce hydrogen consumption rate by 1.34%–2.45%, suppress the state of charge (SOC) fluctuations, and enhance operational efficiency by 2.43%–5.56%. While inheriting global optimization capabilities, the proposed strategy significantly enhances rapid response and adaptive capacity under complex operational conditions, which significantly improves the economic performance and operational stability of aviation fuel cell hybrid power systems.

item.title: Toward Smart Laboratories: A Robotic Gripper Integrating MSSPP Sensing for Simultaneous Grasping Monitoring and Material Identification
item.description: The operation in high-risk laboratory environments, such as biochemistry and materials synthesis, often exposes humans to various hazardous substances. Alternatively, intelligent robots with multidimensional tactile sensors are frequently studied. However, it remains challenging to offer the capability of material identification, while maintaining the tactile sensing within the same compact device. In this study, we developed an intelligent perception system integrated into a robotic gripper with a magneto-spoof surface plasmon polariton (MSSPP) sensor. This system simultaneously performs grasping monitoring and material identification. It enables real-time force sensing via a silicone converter and phase-sensitive detection, and realizes noncontact identification of materials in ten types of centrifuge tubes by analyzing microwave dielectric responses within the 4.78∼4.94 GHz band. Machine learning algorithms are also applied to assist classification. Experimental results demonstrate its high sensitivity to both mechanical and dielectric parameters. The proposed sensor offers a multimodal, compact, and cross-media sensing technique for intelligent robots and robotic teleoperation in high-risk laboratory environments.

item.title: Adaptive Optimal Output Regulation Based on Adaptive Dynamic Programming and Output-Feedback Hybrid Iteration: Theory and Applications Across Diverse Time Scales From PMDC Motor Drives to IBR-Based Microgrids
item.description: This article investigates the adaptive optimal output-feedback control problem for discrete-time multiagent linear systems. An adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) algorithm, hybrid iteration (HI), is proposed to solve the adaptive optimal output-feedback control problem. The primary contribution of this work is the advancement of an approach to addressing adaptive optimal output regulation problems for multiagent systems via output-feedback control. Unlike existing ADP-based strategies, such as policy iteration (PI) and value iteration (VI), the proposed output-feedback HI strategy learns the optimal output-feedback control policy over two phases. In the first phase, a data-driven scheme is deployed to learn an admissible output-feedback control policy based on online data. In the second phase, given the admissible control policy, the optimal output-feedback control policy is learned via PI with an accelerated convergence rate. Illustrative examples demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed output-feedback HI approach to controlling systems with slow and fast dynamics, including long and short time scales (or time constants), respectively, are provided and studied. In this regard, experimental results from rapid control prototyping of a permanent-magnet DC motor drive utilizing a DC–DC buck converter (as an example of a system with slow dynamics, or equivalently, with long time scales) are presented. Additionally, testing results from power hardware-in-the-loop simulations of a modern microgrid utilizing inverter-based resources (as an example of a system with fast dynamics, or equivalently, with short time scales) reveal the efficacy and practicality of the proposed ADP-based adaptive optimal output regulation employing HI.

item.title: Integrated Attack-Defense Framework for Minecart Suspension Systems: Polynomial-Driven Flexibility Enhancement and HIL Experimental Validation
item.description: This article centers on constructing an integrated attack-defense framework for maliciously compromised minecart active suspension systems (MASSs) amid the advancement of network and communication technologies. First, in view of the attackers’ limited energy budget, a membership drift-dependent dynamic-intensity (MDD) attack model is developed. With the exfiltration of key system information, the attacker can assess the system state via the degree of membership drift and dynamically tune the attack intensity to achieve maximum damage. Second, by virtue of homogeneous polynomial techniques, an attack-pattern-detection-guided redundancy compensation (ARC) defense mechanism is devised correspondingly. Through the deployment of redundant transmission paths, this scheme enables the reachability of critical information via auxiliary paths, even if the primary channel is sabotaged by adversarial attacks. Moreover, to mitigate the asynchrony in attack mode observation under practical conditions, a probabilistic detection framework is introduced to characterize imperfect mode matching. On this basis, dynamic compensation is implemented by leveraging the exceptional flexibility of gain scheduling within the polynomial framework. Finally, software simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the obtained results.

item.title: A Linear Irradiance Control Power Supply for Dielectric Barrier Discharge-Based 222 nm Excimer Ultraviolet Lamps
item.description: The 222 nm excimer ultraviolet (UV) lamp emerges as a promising disinfection technology because it is harmless to human bodies. However, existing power supplies fail to achieve linear irradiance control due to the complexity of the irradiation process and indeterminate load characteristics, resulting in limited use in high-precision applications. The dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) and radiation principles of 222 nm excimer UV lamps are analyzed in this study, and the piecewise linearization load model of excimer UV lamps is established. A linear irradiance control power supply for 222 nm excimer UV lamps is proposed. The power supply consists of four parts: the flyback circuit, the LCC resonant circuit, the feedback loop, and the UV lamp load. The LCC resonant converter designed by the capacitive characteristics of UV lamps can filter out higher order harmonics and prevent voltage distortion. The irradiance of the excimer UV lamp is linearly controlled by controlling the frequency of the resonant converter, and a sine output voltage waveform with a constant peak value of 4 kV is obtained through a flyback circuit with a feedback loop. Besides, in order to verify the proposed control, a simulation model is established by using SIMPLIS software. Finally, a linear irradiance control power supply prototype is implemented to verify the feasibility of the proposed method, and the coefficient R2 of determination for evaluating irradiance linearity is 0.9996.

item.title: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Harmonic Mitigation Strategy for Renewable Energy Distribution Network Based on Two-Stage Dynamic Partition
item.description: To mitigate the dispersed and time-varying harmonics in renewable energy distribution networks, this article proposes a cloud-edge collaborative harmonic mitigation strategy based on a two-stage dynamic partition method. First, an improved PageRank algorithm observation node selection method is proposed to select suitable observation nodes. The observation nodes can effectively represent the harmonic level of the entire network, thereby reducing the complexity of optimizing mitigation parameters. Second, the mitigation capabilities of mitigation devices, such as the voltage-detection-based active power filter (VDAPF) and multifunctional grid-connected inverters (MFGCI), are limited and cannot cover the time-varying harmonics across the entire network. To address this issue, a two-stage dynamic partition method based on multiple partition indicators is proposed to dynamically divide the distribution network into several areas. Then, the mitigation areas of VDAPF and MFGCI are accurately determined based on the cloud-edge collaborative technology. Finally, a multitimescale collaborative optimization mitigation strategy is proposed to optimize the mitigation parameters of the mitigation devices. In addition, an improved NSGA-II multiobjective optimization algorithm is proposed to correct the mitigation parameters to improve the mitigation effectiveness during the short-term scale optimization process. Using the IEEE-33 bus system as a case study, the simulation and experimental results indicate that the proposed mitigation strategy can quickly and efficiently mitigate the time-varying harmonics of the distribution network.

item.title: A Novel Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Current Behavior for SRD System Considering Multifault Features
item.description: To enhance the reliability of switched reluctance machine drive (SRD) systems, this article proposes a novel fault diagnosis method focusing on current behavior analysis to identify faults in power switches, diodes, windings, and current sensors. By employing a novel sensor placement strategy and a precise current reconstruction algorithm, this method enables real-time monitoring of each component within the SRD system without additional hardware. The proposed method features a simple structure that is independent of control methods, allowing for comprehensive diagnosis of 12 fault types across six categories within as few as one to four control cycles. Through experimental verification, the proposed method exhibits its robustness and fast response, demonstrating the applicability in various SRD environments.

item.title: PE-TSFM: Self-Supervised Time-Series Learning for Generalizable Power Converter Health Monitoring Under Unseen Conditions
item.description: Data-driven health monitoring of power converters remains limited by poor generalization to unseen operating conditions. This work addresses this out-of-distribution (OOD) challenge by building a domain-specific time-series foundation model (PE-TSFM) that learns representations directly from large-scale unlabeled converter data. Unlike generic TSFMs trained on broad time-series datasets, the proposed PE-TSFM is pretrained entirely on domain data, enabling it to learn the physical relationships unique to power electronics. To further tailor the model to this domain, we introduce a dual-attention mechanism that captures both temporal patterns and inter-channel dependencies. While generic TSFMs primarily model temporal dependencies, the added channel attention (CA) captures inter-sensor physical relationships essential for converter degradation analysis. A dataset containing 141 million unlabeled timestamps from an operating power converter is used for pretraining. Experiments show that PE-TSFMs achieve 76%–92% accuracy under unseen operating conditions. In contrast, generic TSFMs achieve around 60% and conventional time-series models achieve around 40% accuracy. This result confirms the strong OOD generalization of the proposed PE-TSFM. Ablation studies further verify that the introduced CA mechanism significantly improves model performance. In addition, we conduct detailed studies on model scalability, hyperparameter sensitivity, and interpretability to provide a comprehensive understanding of the proposed approach.

item.title: A Self-Powered Wireless Deformation Sensor System for Monitoring the Expansion Joints of Gas Insulated Switchgear
item.description: In this work, a self-powered wireless deformation sensor system is designed, fabricated, and characterized. The self-powered monitoring is realized by the combination of the low-power operation of a sensor system and energy harvesting from a weak stray magnetic field. The magnetic energy harvester (MEH) is a resonating electromagnetic device based on a cantilever beam structure, capable of generating 113.6 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$W power under a stray magnetic field with a very low amplitude of 50 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$Trms at 50 Hz. The harvested power is used to charge a battery and then power a deformation sensor system with an average operation current of 18.0 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$A and voltage of 3.3 V. Finally, experimental results confirm that the proposed self-powered sensor system can be used to monitor the deformation of an expansion joint on a gas-insulated switchgear (GIS).

item.title: A Universal Photodiode-Based Optical Gate Driver for GaN Power Devices
item.description: Optically controlled power devices hold promise for achieving minimal triggering delay, simplified control for device stacking, and high electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity. Although gallium nitride (GaN) devices are rapidly advancing power electronics applications, optically controlled high-voltage switching has rarely been reported in GaN. This work addresses this gap by presenting a universal, optically controlled gate driver based on two photodiodes (PDs) in a totem-pole structure capable of switching GaN power devices with fast speed and low optical power. The two reverse-biased PDs are controlled by complementary optical signals to provide gate current, emulating a current-source gate driver. The proposed driver is demonstrated on both voltage- and current-driven GaN transistors, including a 650 V GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) and a 1200 V vertical GaN junction-gate field-effect transistor (JFET). The GaN HEMT achieves some of the fastest switching speeds and lowest required optical powers reported for optically controlled power devices. For the current-driven GaN JFET, the PD’s intrinsic properties provide both transient and steady-state gate current, simplifying the driving circuitry and reducing driver losses. An analytical model is further developed to describe the switching dynamics of both devices under PD-based optical control. These results reveal the potential of PD-based optical gate driving schemes for advancing GaN power electronics.

item.title: Novel Dynamic Amplitude Normalization Method Based on Tracking Differentiator for SOGI-FLL
item.description: The second-order generalized integrator-frequency locked loop (SOGI-FLL) is widely applied in power electronic converter control to extract grid voltage amplitude, frequency, and phase. Amplitude normalization is usually incorporated to mitigate errors induced by voltage deviation; however, the increasing integration of new energy sources has reduced grid inertia, leading to more frequent voltage amplitude fluctuations. Traditional SOGI-based normalization suffers from inadequate dynamic performance due to the phase lag of orthogonal signals, degrading SOGI-FLL extraction accuracy. To address this, a dynamic amplitude normalization method based on a tracking differentiator (TD) is proposed. It leverages the phase-leading characteristic of TD to generate strictly orthogonal signals and employs an independent SOGI for input prefiltering to suppress noise interference on TD, thereby achieving accurate amplitude extraction and dynamic normalization. Theoretical analysis and experimental verification show that the proposed method can accurately extract amplitude and frequency information even under voltage amplitude fluctuations and sudden changes, and its performance is superior to the traditional method.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Virtual Inertia Pinning Control for Heterogeneous VSGs
item.description: Inertia coordination among multiple virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) has emerged as a crucial topic for modern low-inertia power systems. However, in practical applications, disparities and fluctuations exist inherently in the rated capacities, network topologies, and intrinsic parameters of VSGs. Additionally, inertia characteristics at their points of common coupling (PCCs) are frequently influenced by other connected devices, and these inconsistencies exacerbate internal disturbances among VSGs during load variations, and even cause oscillations. To tackle this issue, We propose a reinforcement learning-based virtual inertia pinning control (RLVIPC) that achieves coordinated and stable matching among heterogeneous VSGs. Specifically, an optimal inertia dynamic matching mechanism is designed for heterogeneous VSGs to overcome the dynamic performance limitations of conventional fixed-inertia control. A pinning control strategy is proposed to mitigate the curse of dimensionality resulting from separate inertia control of individual VSGs. Furthermore, a reinforcement learning-based optimal inertia tracking algorithm is designed to enable adjustment of inertia and damping coefficients. Verified by simulation and experimental results, the proposed method provides an advantageous solution by suppressing oscillations and simplifying control complexity.

item.title: Decoupled Controllable-Boundary Model and Coordinated Voltage Support for Renewable Power Plants With Multiple IBRs Under Asymmetric LVRT
item.description: Large-scale renewable power plants (RPPs) should coordinate numerous differentiated inverter-based resources (IBRs) to provide reliable voltage support under low-voltage ride-through (LVRT). Yet the reactive-power controllable boundary (RCB) of multiple IBRs under asymmetric LVRT remains insufficiently explored, limiting support capability and risking local over-voltage. This study develops a unified RCB model that considers the impacts of interactive coupling, phase-locking deviation, and voltage propagation. Then, four tight constraints are derived from RCB vector trajectories on the complex domain plane to shrink the original RCB equations, yielding a linear and decoupled minimum RCB intersection under various fault conditions. The minimum RCB can regulate the conservative distribution of sequence voltage boundaries allowed for each bus based on the RPP's pre-event state. During LVRT, a coordinated voltage support strategy is proposed to distributed adjust reactive outputs of multiple IBRs following an optimal trajectory in the pre-given RCB, which maximizes voltage support capability. The hardware-in-the-loop experiment referred to an actual large-scale RPP project shows that the proposed strategy eliminates local over-voltage risks observed in existing strategies (up to 17.3%) and improves the faulted-phase voltage support capability by 17.48% on average across various fault conditions.

item.title: Preventive Control Optimization Against Voltage Oscillations Induced by Steady-State Repeated LVRT Based on Thevenin Equivalent Parameter Correction
item.description: Accelerated global energy transition towards low-carbon sources drives large-scale renewable integration, posing challenges to energy system security. In multi-renewable energy plants grid-connected systems (MREP-GCSs), repeated low voltage ride-through (LVRT) under steady-state can induce a novel switching oscillation. The oscillation stems from a self-sustaining cycle where, during steady-state operation, under certain grid conditions, increased active power output can trigger LVRT entry, which restores voltage and prompts LVRT exit, only for power restoration to immediately re-trigger the condition, causing persistent switching oscillations. Therefore, an optimized preventive control method is proposed against repeated LVRT, explicitly considering inter-plant influences in MREP-GCSs. Firstly, an assessment framework based on refined repeated LVRT occurrence conditions is developed. The re-derivation of this condition is based on equivalent parameters at the point of common coupling (PCC), considering the mutual power-voltage coupling between plants to correct the equivalent voltage. Secondly, a preventive control optimization method for repeated LVRT is developed from the perspective of online preventive control. To achieve precise regulation, a quantitative relationship between system-wide regulation variables combination and repeated LVRT boundary is established, along with other operating conditions, to form the constraints of the optimization model. The objective function aims to minimize regulation costs by coordinating grid-side and plant-side controls. This system-level method addresses the multi-plant boundary effects of control variables for coordinated multi-PCC control, optimizing grid-plant co-regulation to ensure renewable energy accommodation and enhance stability. Simulation results demonstrate the method accurately identifies repeated LVRT scenarios and suppresses oscillations.

item.title: Optimal Sizing of Energy Storage Systems for Grid-Forming Wind Turbines in Offshore Wind Farms
item.description: The high penetration of inverter-based resources, such as wind turbines (WTs), threatens power system stability due to their lack of inherent inertia. Therefore, equipping WTs with energy storage systems (ESSs) under grid-forming control, such as a virtual synchronous generator (VSG), is a promising solution. However, optimal ESS sizing remains challenging due to the wind stochasticity and the intricate coupling dynamics of VSGs. To address this challenge, this study proposes a stochastic dynamic optimization framework for ESS sizing in offshore wind farms (OWFs). Specifically, a unified frequency response model is developed using stochastic differential equations, explicitly incorporating Itô-process-based wind dynamics and the coupling between VSG voltage behavior and OWF power flow. On this basis, a stochastic dynamic optimization model is constructed to determine optimal ESS power and energy ratings. The key to converting this model into a tractable deterministic convex program lies in approximating stochastic expectations with Taylor-series-based assessment functions. To enable efficient large-scale optimization, the proposed framework employs a temporal decomposition strategy combined with the alternating direction method of multipliers. Simulations on a 36-turbine OWF validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, yielding an optimal ESS configuration with a power rating of 689–697 kW and an energy capacity of 19.88–19.95 kWh. Moreover, the solution strategy achieves a 77.9% reduction in solution time with only a 0.44% increase in the objective value.

item.title: Shaping the Q-U Droop Characteristic of Grid-Forming Converters From the Perspective of Constant Voltage Control
item.description: With the increasing penetration rate of variable renewable energy (VRE) and other inverter-based resources (IBR) in power systems, system inertia and strength are being continuously weakened. Grid-forming (GFM) technology, adaptable to weak grids, has attracted widespread attention. The GFM Q-U droop control is widely adopted in practice, but it is challenging to tune key parameters, such as initial voltage reference value and droop coefficient, therefore, the adaptability and effectiveness of voltage support is difficult to ensure. To take the advantages of GFM converters as voltage sources, adopting constant voltage control (CVC) seems to be a better choice. This paper clarifies the implicit internal connection between CVC and droop control, indicating that the droop characteristic does not inherently depend on droop control, but should be regarded as a natural external port performance under internal CVC.
