The estimated dq-admittance models are further applied to generalized Nyquist stability analysis and validated against EMT time-domain simulations under multiple operating points and grid-strength conditions.

item.title: Online Feasible Region Characterization of Aggregated DERs via Incremental Projection
item.description: Performing fast and accurate feasible region characterization (FRC) for aggregated distributed energy resources (DERs) is essential for real-time operational dispatching. Affected by the temporal coupling and the uncertainty associated with DERs, the aggregated feasible regions exhibit high-dimensional coupling and strong stochasticity. However, existing methods cannot quickly perform accurate FRC of the entire operational domain, resulting in preventing real-time updating of FRC based on rolling forecasts of uncertain sources and loads. To this end, an incremental projection-based online full-time-domain FRC method is proposed in this paper, which requires only a local projection of the forecasts to achieve fast and accurate FRC. First, the reversible decoupling equivalent reformulation is developed to decompose the original high-dimensional FRC into several sliced low-dimensional FRCs, while the temporal coupling feature is retained. Then, to shorten the computation time, a universal incremental projection paradigm is constructed, in which the whole FRC is quickly updated by replacing local projections in the complete FRC results obtained offline. Statistical analysis validates that the proposed method can reduce the computation time in the order of 0.55% compared to that of the existing techniques without losing accuracy.

item.title: Physically Consistent Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) for Microgrid Identification and Real-Time Frequency Control
item.description: This paper proposes PC-SINDYc, a novel framework for the identification and frequency control of microgrids (MGs) with distributed energy resources. By leveraging physics-guided library construction, total least squares regression, and random sample consensus, the regression algorithm of PC-SINDYc robustly identifies the true frequency dynamics of MGs from phasor measurement unit (PMU) data, considering noise, delays, and constraint activations. Based on the identified model, the PC-SINDYc framework further incorporates a model predictive controller (MPC) for real-time frequency control. We prove that, under mild conditions, PC-SINDYc ensures asymptotic stability of the MG. Simulations on 4-bus and 13-bus MGs demonstrate that PC-SINDYc effectively controls MG’s frequency across various disturbances unseen during the offline identification, outperforming PI controllers, conventional SINDYc, and state-of-the-art reinforcement learning methods.

item.title: Hybrid Attention-Augmented Self-Interpretable Channel-Grouped Graph Convolutional Network for Robust Distribution Network Fault Diagnosis
item.description: Deep learning (DL)-based methods have illustrated excellent performance in distribution network fault diagnosis. However, the “opaque” nature of DL models hinders grid operators from understanding the decision-making processes of these models, affecting model trustworthiness and robustness in diversified diagnosis applications. This paper proposes a hybrid attention-augmented self-interpretable channel-grouped graph convolutional network (HASIG) for diverse short-circuit fault diagnosis of distribution networks, including binary fault detection, faulted line identification, and fault type classification. A channel-grouped graph convolutional network is proposed to learn features from three-phase voltage and current measurements. We present a hybrid attention that combines global edge attention and channel-grouped attention, which can augment the critical features with faithful and robust interpretations during model training, enabling users to gain insights into the predictive behavior inside the model. These three short-circuit fault diagnosis tasks are collaboratively trained under a multi-task learning architecture with interpretable loss constraints. Experiments were conducted on the IEEE 33-bus, IEEE 33-bus with distributed energy resources, and IEEE 123-bus systems with randomized fault parameters. The results show that HASIG achieves competitive diagnostic performance and good interpretability, and demonstrates strong robustness under noisy and missing-data conditions.

item.title: Enhancing Power Distribution System Resilience Through Insurance Mechanisms: An Insurer Optimization Approach With V2G Aggregator Participation
item.description: Current approaches to enhancing system resilience, which prioritize the asset allocation and emergency scheduling optimization, may face challenges related to inadequate asset availability and insufficient, inequitable response capabilities. To address these challenges, this paper designs an insurance mechanism to enhance the resilience of power distribution systems against extreme events. The strategic behavior of the insurer regarding insurance provision and asset aggregation is modeled under a risk-based decision-making framework to maximize the effectiveness of the insurer mechanism. A cooperative framework is formulated to incentivize the emergency service provision from the V2G-capable vehicle aggregator (V2GA). The optimal insurance provisions are determined by addressing the user-insurer-V2GA negotiation process through a tailored two-level nested alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Specifically, the outer ADMM coordinates user–insurer contract negotiation, the inner ADMM handles insurer-V2GA coordination, and the Nash bargaining theory is employed for profit allocation between the insurer and the V2GA. Numerical results verify that the proposed insurer optimization approach could offer a promising solution to enhance system resilience against extreme events.

item.title: Distributed Resilient Power Control Strategy Against Data Injection Attacks in Wind Farms
item.description: With the increasing proportion of installed wind power capacity in the power grid, higher requirements are put forward for the cyber security technology of wind energy enterprises. However, due to problems such as incomplete construction and unstrict requirements, there exist many blind spots of cyber security in the current power monitoring system of wind energy enterprises. Data injection attacks targeting the communication pathway between the supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system and the wind turbines will degrade the power generation of wind farms and lead to an imbalance in the power supply to the grid. To this end, this paper attempts to propose an observation and compensation based distributed resilient power control strategy to resist data injection attacks in the wind farm. The data injection threat model is formulated to characterize the behavior of tampering with the power information of wind turbines reported to the local controller and SCADA system, and an adaptive observer is proposed to observe the injected value in real-time, guiding the wind farm to balance the power generation. A distributed resilient power control strategy is developed to ensure the dynamic balance of expected power generation and the secure operation of wind farms. Extensive studies on a wind farm consisting of 9 wind turbines verify that the proposed method can eliminate the impact of data injection attacks and ensure the expected control performance of the wind farm.

item.title: Secure Prespecified-Time Distributed Energy Management via Dual-Layer Privacy-Preserving Mechanism
item.description: This paper investigates the energy management (EM) problem for microgrids in a fast and secure manner. To rapidly obtain the optimal power output combination, a flexible distributed EM algorithm over digraphs is proposed based on a novel prespecified-time convergence lemma, which enables the presetting of convergence time independent of initial states or algorithmic parameters. Considering the privacy protection of incremental costs (ICs), a new dual-layer privacy-preserving mechanism is devised to defend against both internal honest-but-curious (HBC) distributed generators and external eavesdroppers. The first privacy-preserving layer is state decomposition, which operates throughout the entire scheduling horizon. The second privacy-preserving layer is edge-based additive perturbations, which operates during the coordinated scrambling phase. The state decomposition mechanism divides the ICs into two auxiliary variables, and the additive perturbation method can further protect the privacy of these auxiliary variables. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EM strategy.

item.title: A Probabilistic Graph Reinforcement Learning for Resilient Service Restoration via Microgrid Formation
item.description: Service restoration in distribution systems after major outages is a complex and time-sensitive task under significant uncertainty and high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs). Conventional deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods typically rely on Markov decision processes (MDPs) and Euclidean state representations, limiting their ability to capture stochastic temporal dynamics and network topology. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a probabilistic graph reinforcement learning framework for microgrid formation. The restoration problem is formulated as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) to explicitly model stochastic state sojourn times. A Bayesian graph convolutional network is developed to jointly capture spatial dependencies and parameter uncertainty. Building on this, a novel Bayesian graph soft actor-critic (BGSAC) algorithm is proposed, where the entropy regularization coefficient is adaptively adjusted based on uncertainty estimates, enhancing exploration capability and robustness in uncertain environments. Experimental results on the IEEE 123-bus system demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing DRL approaches in convergence stability and final performance. Moreover, compared with optimization-based and heuristic baselines, it achieves comparable restoration effectiveness with substantially reduced decision time, highlighting its suitability for real-time service restoration.

item.title: Certificate-Guided UAV Sensing for Executable Risk-Limiting OPF in PV-Rich Distribution Systems
item.description: High photovoltaic (PV) penetration motivates risk-limiting optimal power flow (RL-OPF) for voltage-secure distribution operation, yet practical deployment is often hindered by information degradation: sparse measurements, communication outages, and model mismatch inflate the effective disturbance in sensitivity-based feeder models, causing conservative curtailment and second-order cone programming (SOCP) infeasibility. This paper proposes an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled information–control co-optimization framework that treats mobile sensing as an active uncertainty-shaping resource for RL-OPF. A statistically feasible uncertainty set is calibrated from rolling residual samples to yield a tractable SOCP RL-OPF with finite-sample confidence guarantees. A feasibility-oriented risk certificate guides limited UAV sensing toward near-binding constraint directions, and the acquired information is fused through Kalman filter/recursive least squares (KF/RLS) updates for constraint-aligned set reconstruction. Case studies on a modified three-phase IEEE 33-bus PV-rich feeder demonstrate improved executability and utilization without weakening voltage security. Under medium uncertainty, infeasibility drops from 14.8% to 1.8% and daily PV curtailment decreases from 1.58 to 0.79 MWh. Under high uncertainty and 10% topology error, infeasibility decreases from 28.6% to 6.1% and from 41.2% to 11.7%, respectively. Sensitivity results further confirm that a small UAV fleet captures most of the benefit while maintaining out-of-sample voltage risk near the target level.

item.title: Vulnerability of Time-Series AI Detectors to Physics-Informed Poisoning Attacks
item.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been extensively integrated into smart grids to enhance anomaly detection, with time-series AI detectors such as Long Short-Term Memory Autoencoders (LSTM-AE) and Convolutional Autoencoders (Conv-AE) emerging as pivotal technologies for handling sequential data and intricate temporal dependencies. However, this integration exposes critical infrastructure to novel security vulnerabilities, particularly during the model training phase. This paper investigates an underexplored threat: black-box training-data poisoning attacks on time-series AI detectors in power systems. Unlike gradient-based test-time evasion attacks such as the Fast Gradient Sign Method and Carlini & Wagner, our attack is formulated as a black-box training-data corruption framework that poisons archived load records before detector training. We introduce a physics-informed attack framework that leverages Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) to generate physically plausible poisoned load records. The methodology encompasses empirical SDE parameter extraction, template-based synthetic load generation with daily drift compensation, and its integration into an Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system to systematically contaminate the training dataset. Simulation results reveal that time-series AI detectors trained on this tainted data exhibit profound detection failures, misclassifying severe anomalies—such as system frequency drops below 49.5 Hz—as normal operations, thereby underscoring a critical vulnerability in AI-enabled power systems and the urgent need for defenses against such physics-constrained adversarial threats.

item.title: EVEsecCOM: A Safety and Security Protection Approach for the Emergency Electricity Supply With Electric Vehicles
item.description: With the rapid growth of electricity consumption, the power grid struggles to balance supply and demand, rendering it unable to cope with emergent electricity shortages. The electric vehicle (EV) features communication, energy storage, and high mobility, enabling it to respond quickly to an emergent electricity supply event. However, gathering a large number of EVs to supply electricity in a short time presents challenges: First, the lack of standardized EV charging interfaces leads to mismatches, posing physical safety risks; Second, the open communication network used to coordinate EVs is vulnerable to cyberattacks. To mitigate these risks, we introduce EVEsecCOM, an integrated approach that addresses both physical safety and communication security. EVs are grouped and summoned by charging interface type to ensure safe electricity transmission. Communication security is achieved through chameleon hash functions combined with symmetric encryption, while the EV-call protocol merges key agreement and identity authentication to minimize overhead. Formal and informal security analyses confirm resilience against replay, impersonation, tampering, and privacy inference attacks. Compared with the latest related protocols in terms of communication and computation costs, our proposed protocol is shown to be superior. Subsequently, we conducted batch experiments on physical interface grouping and intra-group operation computation costs. Finally, we conduct simulation experiments in NS-3 to test the performance of the proposed protocol.

item.title: A Causal-Guided Multimodal Large Language Model for Generalized Power System Time-Series Data Analytics
item.description: Power system time series analytics is critical in understanding the system operation conditions and predicting the future trends. Despite the wide adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, many AI-based time series analytical models suffer from task-specificity (i.e., one model for one task) and structural rigidity (i.e., the input-output format is fixed), leading to limited model performance and resource waste. In this paper, we propose a Causal-Guided Multimodal Large Language Model (CM-LLM) that can solve heterogeneous power system time-series analysis tasks. First, we introduce a physics-statistics combined causal discovery mechanism to capture the causal relationship, which is represented by a graph, among power system variables. Second, we propose a multimodal data preprocessing framework that can encode and fuse text, graph and time series to enhance the model performance. Last, we formulate a generic “mask-and-reconstruct” paradigm and design a dynamic input-output padding mechanism to enable CM-LLM to adapt to heterogeneous time-series analysis tasks with varying sample lengths. Simulation results based on open-source LLM Qwen and real-world datasets demonstrate that, after simple fine-tuning, the proposed CM-LLM can achieve satisfying accuracy and efficiency on three heterogeneous time-series analytics tasks: missing data imputation, forecasting and super resolution.

item.title: A Graph Neural Network With Auxiliary Task Learning for Missing PMU Data Reconstruction
item.description: In wide-area measurement systems (WAMS), phasor measurement unit (PMU) measurement is prone to data missing due to hardware failures, communication delays, and cyber-attacks. Existing data-driven methods are limited by poor adaptability to concept drift in power systems, poor robustness under high missing rates, and reliance on the unrealistic assumption of full system observability. Thus, this paper proposes an auxiliary task learning (ATL) method for reconstructing missing PMU data. First, a K-hop graph neural network (GNN) is proposed to enable direct learning on the subgraph consisting of PMU nodes, overcoming the limitation of the incompletely observable system. Then, an auxiliary learning framework consisting of two complementary graph networks is designed for accurate reconstruction: a spatial-temporal GNN extracts spatial-temporal dependencies from PMU data to reconstruct missing values, and another auxiliary GNN utilizes the low-rank property of PMU data to achieve unsupervised online learning. In this way, the low-rank properties of the PMU data are dynamically leveraged across the architecture to ensure robustness and self-adaptation. Numerical results demonstrate the superior offline and online performance of the proposed method under high missing rates and incomplete observability.

item.title: Physics-Guided Data-Driven Power Flow Modeling for Unbalanced Distribution Feeders Without Phasor Measurements
item.description: Accurate power-flow (PF) modeling in medium-voltage distribution feeders is challenging due to incomplete physical parameters, for which data-driven approaches provide a flexible and effective solution. However, available data are mostly scalar measurements from transformer low-voltage sides without phase angles. In three-phase three-wire (3P3W) feeders, strong inter-phase coupling caused by line mutual impedances and transformer connections further limits the accuracy of purely data-driven models. Although physics-guided methods have demonstrated strong robustness to measurement errors in vector-domain modeling, effective mechanisms for incorporating physical guidance under scalar measurements are still lacking. To address this gap, this paper proposes a physics-guided data-driven scalar PF model. The model establishes equivalent scalar mappings that characterize feeder and transformer coupling, embedding this physical guidance into the data-driven regression process. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy, robustness, and physical consistency, ensuring reliable PF estimation even under large measurement errors and strong phase-coupling conditions.

item.title: Trustworthy Reinforcement Learning for Renewable Base Energy Management Against Communication Failures
item.description: Renewable energy integration introduces volatility, posing significant challenges to power systems energy management. Conventional methods struggle to handle the volatility relying on high-fidelity models. Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) offers an alternative by learning control policies based on environment interaction. However, communication failures and MW-scale renewable volatility cause delayed state perception and cascaded constraint violations, threatening both system reliability and economic efficiency, and limiting RL deployment. We formulate a communication-failure-tolerant DRL (CFT-DRL) framework that considers the grid-consistent belief state and physically operational envelopes simultaneously. A state belief estimation module is designed to alleviate state perception bias caused by communication failures. An operational-envelope-embedded mechanism is developed to incorporate operational envelopes into policy updates, complemented by a security execution layer to ensure strict constraint satisfaction. Considering the efficient learning and deployment feasibility, we align the policy exploration with physical state transitions. Comparative studies demonstrate superior robustness, operational feasibility, and readiness for practical deployment of the proposed method.

item.title: A Data-Driven Probabilistic Harmonic Current Forecasting for Aggregated Harmonic Sources
item.description: With the increasing deployment of non-linear power electronic devices in distribution networks, the issue of excessive harmonics has become increasingly prominent. Accurate analysis and forecasting of harmonic currents are essential to better understand and mitigate harmonic-related problems. Common harmonic sources in power grids include various types of loads and renewable energy generation equipment, such as wind and photovoltaic systems. Accordingly, this paper focuses on forecasting harmonic currents for different types of aggregated harmonic sources. Considering the strong randomness, high time-variability, and coupling characteristics of harmonic currents, a data-driven probabilistic harmonic current forecasting method is proposed. First, the raw data are decomposed into deterministic and stochastic components. Next, a radial basis function autoregressive exponential model is employed to perform point forecasting of the deterministic component, accommodating multiple input factors and simultaneous multi-harmonic outputs while preserving model partial interpretability. Subsequently, the proposed multi-Gaussian fitting method and an improved Markov chain Monte Carlo approach are used for probabilistic forecasting of the stochastic component. Finally, the deterministic and stochastic component predictions are combined to yield the final probabilistic harmonic current forecast. Using actual harmonic measurement data, comparative analyses with multiple intelligent models are conducted to validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed forecasting method. Furthermore, the harmonic current predictions are applied to forward probabilistic harmonic power flows, and corresponding forward and new probabilistic harmonic mitigation measures are proposed, demonstrating practical engineering applicability.

item.title: A Two-Stage Topology-Adaptive Physics-Guided Power Flow Learning Approach for Power Distribution Networks
item.description: Data-driven methods have shown promising performance in accelerating power flow (PF) calculation for power distribution networks (PDNs). However, with complex operational uncertainties, modern PDNs involve frequent topology variations. These variations alter network constraints and thus change the PF mapping, making models trained on specific topologies biased under new configurations. Moreover, due to limited monitoring in PDNs, sufficient labeled data are difficult to collect after topology changes, making direct retraining prone to overfitting. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a two-stage topology-adaptive physics-guided PF learning framework for PDNs. In the first stage, impedance-aware graph attention models are trained on historical topologies to learn topology-specific residual mappings between AC power flow (ACPF) and linear coupled power flow (LCPF) solutions. These historical models provide informative predictions for target-topology adaptation. In the second stage, for target topologies with limited samples, nonparametric Gaussian process regression (GPR) is performed in a node-wise manner to fuse the historical predictions with the LCPF solutions. Simulation results on the 33-node, 69-node, and 118-node systems demonstrate high accuracy and topology adaptability across radial, meshed, and islanded structures with limited target samples.

item.title: Physics-Embedded Graph Convolutional Network With Topology-Adaptive Transfer Learning for Power Flow Prediction
item.description: Power flow prediction is a growing task in uncertain power system operation and analysis. Although data-driven models which apply machine learning techniques offer computational efficiency for power flow calculation, they often result in physically inconsistent solutions and exhibit poor generalization across different network topologies. This article proposes a physics-embedded graph convolutional network (PE-GCN) for physically consistent power flow prediction, and further develops a topology-adaptive transfer learning framework to improve generalization across different power network topologies. PE-GCN is developed based on a reformulated bus injection model (BIM) and embeds physical laws into the network architecture and training process. Specifically, hard constraints are enforced through a nodal power balance correction layer, and soft constraints are incorporated during training via a physics-regularized loss to enhance physical consistency. Building on PE-GCN, a topology-adaptive transfer learning framework with adversarial domain adaptation is introduced to improve generalization across network topologies and reduce the reliance on extensive labeled data under topology variations. Numerical studies on the IEEE-30, IEEE-118, and IEEE-300 bus systems validate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of prediction accuracy, physical consistency, computational efficiency, and adaptability to topology variations.

item.title: Decision-Focused Learning With Machine Learning Proxies for Energy Storage Systems
item.description: As electricity prices become increasingly volatile due to the growing penetration of renewable energy sources, Energy Storage Systems (ESS) are encountering greater opportunities for inter-temporal arbitrage. These can be harnessed through participation in electricity markets using a predict-then-optimize framework: a forecasting model first predicts prices, which are subsequently used in a profit maximization problem. Decision-Focused Learning (DFL) techniques, allowing to train forecasters to directly maximize profits of optimized decisions rather than minimizing statistical price forecasting errors, have been shown to increase profits. However, these techniques are computationally inefficient because they require solving the optimization problem across the entire training set for each training epoch. To address this issue, we introduce a machine learning proxy method mimicking the output of the optimization problem during training. Our approach leverages duality theory to retrieve decisions in two steps: 1) predicting a key dual variable with a pre-trained neural network, and 2) applying smoothing functions to this prediction to determine the ESS (dis)charge decisions. In a case study involving an ESS participating in the day-ahead market with real-life data, we demonstrate that our proxy method significantly reduces training time compared to benchmark DFL methods, while achieving comparable or superior out-of-sample profits.

item.title: Vision of Future Smart Control Center: Fusion of Large Language Models and Power System Intelligent Computing
item.description: The high stochasticity of renewable dominated power grids demands advanced dispatch strategies. However, the disparity between flexible operator intent and rigid legacy tools hinders resilient system operation. To address this challenge,this paper proposes a future smart control center architecture that fuses Large Language Models (LLMs) with Power System Intelligent Computing (PSIC). In this architecture, the LLM functions as the cognitive core for intent understanding, workflow orchestration, and causal reasoning. Concurrently, PSIC executes physical simulations and data-driven optimization tasks decomposed by the LLM. This integration creates a cognitive decision-making process where the adaptive decision-making capability enabled by LLM is rigorously bounded and verified by physical laws. Consequently, the architecture enables next generation human-machine collaborative dispatch, advancing grid operations from automation toward true intelligence and self-evolution.

item.title: Learning a Unified Feasibility--Cost Interface for Heterogeneous Flexible Resources
item.description: With the rapid proliferation of heterogeneous flexible resources (HFRs), such as microgrids and virtual power plants, hierarchical dispatch has become essential, making aggregate modeling a crucial foundation for resource coordination. Existing methods typically decouple the aggregate feasible region (AFR) of HFRs from the aggregate cost function (ACF). This separation isolates physical constraints from economic signals, preventing operators from quantifying the marginal value of flexibility and causing modeling redundancy. To solve this, we propose a feasibility-embedded aggregate cost function, unifying feasibility and cost into a strictly convex scalar interface. First, by implicitly representing physical limits as steep economic penalties, we recast the decoupled aggregation of AFR and ACF into a unified fitting problem. Second, a tailored multi-scale input-convex neural network is developed to resolve the inherent conflict between approximating smooth operational costs and capturing sharp feasibility barriers. Numerical results validate that the proposed interface achieves superior accuracy while maintaining a highly compact formulation.

item.title: Learning-Augmented Mixed-Integer Reformulation for Dynamic Traffic and Energy Assignment in Spatio-Temporal V2G Coordination
item.description: The increasing integration of electric vehicles (EVs) enables grid services through spatio-temporal vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology. While prior studies have explored dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) for EV charging management, most existing DTA formulations treat charging and discharging power as exogenous or fixed parameters, limiting V2G flexibility utilization and coordination. This work proposes a learning-augmented mixed-integer reformulation for dynamic traffic and energy assignment (DTEA) that co-optimizes EV traffic flows and continuous (dis)charging power. Specifically, to address the nonlinear flow-power coupling terms, we develop a structure-preserving constraint learning-based method that replicates only the nonlinear coupling terms while retaining the operational constraints. The trained neural networks (NNs) are embedded into the optimization model through tractable mixed-integer reformulations, and data-driven local trust-region restrictions are introduced to mitigate extrapolation risk and improve solution reliability. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and robustness of the proposed solution method.

item.title: Priority Random Access and Power Control for NOMA-ALOHA in Heterogeneous mMTC
item.description: This paper presents a novel priority random access (PRA) non-orthogonal multiple access assisted ALOHA, called PRA-NA, to provide access priority for machine-type devices (MTDs) with different delay requirements (i.e., delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant). We first introduce a received power level model that incorporates imperfect channel state information and imperfect successive interference cancellation to study the impact of practical non-ideal channel conditions. Two PRA strategies including fixed PRA-NA (FPRA-NA) and adaptive PRA-NA (APRA-NA) are then designed to reduce the average access delay of delay-sensitive MTDs in heterogeneous massive machine-type communications. Subsequently, the throughputs of both the FPRA-NA and APRA-NA strategies are analyzed to demonstrate their effectiveness. Moreover, to improve the energy efficiency of random access, we introduce an enhanced user barring algorithm (EUBA) to carry out power control. It is shown that our proposed EUBA can not only alleviate the user overload problem, but also reduce the average transmit power of MTDs. By extending it to the proposed PRA-NA schemes, we demonstrate via extensive simulation results that the random access performances in terms of throughput, access delay, and energy efficiency can be significantly improved over the conventional NOMA-ALOHA.

item.title: Joint Resource Allocation in Vehicular Networks Based on Multi-Round Emergent Communication With Dynamic Reward
item.description: Emerging vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks increasingly rely on air–ground integrated architectures to enable reliable, low-latency, and high-throughput communication in complex and dynamic environments. Nevertheless, distributed resource allocation in such networks remains challenging, as agents' limited observability and the constrained adaptability of existing communication mechanisms make efficient distributed coordination difficult. Moreover, the energy constraints of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) further degrade the system's service continuity and training stability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that integrates multi-round emergent communication and dynamic reward weighting for joint spectrum and power allocation. Through multi-round message exchanges among cooperative agents, the proposed communication mechanism enhances global awareness and coordination efficiency in distributed environments, while the dynamic reward design improves UAV energy adaptability and system robustness under constrained power conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared with baseline methods across energy efficiency, transmission success rate, and service continuity.

item.title: Uplink Performance of RIS-Assisted Multi-Cell Massive MIMO Systems Jointly RIS Phase Shift Design
item.description: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems in multi-cell scenarios exhibit coherent interference caused by pilot contamination.Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has a promising prospect in the beyond-5G network because the electromagnetic propagation environment can be manipulated by adjusting the phase shift of each reflecting unit.In this paper, we consider a RIS-assisted multi-cell massive MIMO system with spatially correlated channels and analyze the impact of coherent and incoherent interference on performance during the uplink data transmission. First, each base station (BS) estimates the channel based on the uplink pilot information and the minimum mean square error estimator. Then, the spectral efficiency (SE) is computed for a finite number of BS antennas and RIS elements. Based on the SE and uplink signal-to-noise-plus-interference ratio expressions, we analyze the impact of pilot contamination, non-coherent interference, and noise on the system. Furthermore, we design the RIS phase shift to maximize the average power in the target area while minimizing the estimation error. The sum SE maximization problem improves the user SE under the transmit power constraint. Numerical results show that both the RIS phase shift design and data stream power control can improve the system efficiency, especially in poor propagation conditions.

item.title: Hybrid-Field Channel Estimation Based on Manifold Optimization for XL-MIMO: A Proximal Gradient Algorithm on the Fixed/Low-Rank Matrices
item.description: This paper investigates two hybrid-field channel estimation (CE) algorithms for extremely large-scale MIMO systems. Unlike prior compressive sensing-based algorithms relying solely on sparsity, the proposed algorithms address energy leakage caused by the mismatch between the predefined codebook and the actual channel by joint exploitation of channel sparsity and low-rank structure, enabling more precise channel representation. Simultaneously, manifold optimization is employed to enhance the accuracy of the solution, thereby improving the CE performance. Specifically, we analyze the sparse and low-rank representation of hybrid-field channels incorporating both line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight paths. Subsequently, the hybrid-field CE problem is formulated as the sparse matrix recovery problem with fixed-rank/low-rank constraints for known/unknown channel ranks, incorporating an $\ell _{1}$-norm term in the objective function to promote sparsity. Both algorithms employ the proximal operator to address the non-smooth $\ell _{1}$-norm. For solving the sparse matrix recovery problem with the non-convex fixed-rank constraint, the fixed-rank matrix set is regarded as a fixed-rank matrix manifold, and a proximal gradient manifold optimization (PGMO) algorithm is proposed to search for the solution on this manifold. For solving the sparse matrix recovery problem with the non-convex and non-smooth low-rank constraint, a rank-adaptive projected PGMO algorithm is proposed, where a rank-adaptation operation is performed to judge a rank, thereby enabling the algorithm to search effectively on the corresponding fixed-rank matrix manifold. By leveraging manifold optimization, the proposed algorithms effectively address the fixed-rank/low-rank constraint challenges, enhancing CE accuracy. Simulation results confirm their superiority.

item.title: Uplink Performance Analysis of SIM-Enhanced Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Channel Aging and Hardware Impairments
item.description: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) and stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM) are regarded as promising technologies for enhancing the performance of next-generation wireless communication systems. By enabling complex signal processing directly in the electromagnetic wave-domain, SIM provides a promising approach to improve hardware efficiency and reduce the number of active antennas in CF-mMIMO systems, enabling more cost-effective and energy-efficient deployments under practical constraints. Addressing the non-ideal factors in practical communication scenarios, this paper investigates the uplink performance of the SIM-enhanced CF-mMIMO system subject to both channel aging and transceiver hardware impairments. Specifically, we derive a closed-form expression for the uplink achievable spectral efficiency (SE) with large-scale fading decoding (LSFD), quantifying the impacts of these two non-ideal factors. Based on the derived expression, we propose optimization algorithms for SIM wave-domain beamforming and transmit power to further elevate system performance. Firstly, a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based algorithm is designed to efficiently configure the phase shifts of the massive SIM meta-atoms. Then, to accommodate the distinct requirements of maximizing the system sum SE and maximizing the minimum SE, two different power optimization algorithms are developed. Simulation results demonstrate that the uplink SE of the SIM-enhanced CF-mMIMO system significantly outperforms that achieved by the conventional CF-mMIMO system, and validate the effectiveness of the proposed optimization algorithms.

item.title: A Fourier Graph Neural Network-Based Joint Channel Prediction and Beamforming Framework for MISO Systems
item.description: Accurate channel state information (CSI) is indispensable for beamforming in multi-user, multi-antenna systems, as any estimation error directly degrades the downlink signal quality. However, due to the time-varying nature of wireless channels, even CSI obtained through advanced estimation methods can quickly become outdated. This paper proposes a deep learning-based joint channel prediction and beamforming framework for multi-user multiple-input single-output (MISO) downlink transmission. Specifically, we first develop a Fourier Graph Neural Network (FourierGNN)-based channel predictor to obtain future CSI by jointly capturing the spatial and temporal dynamics of wireless channels, thereby alleviating the outdated CSI problem. Based on the predicted CSI, we then construct a joint learning framework to generate the uplink and downlink power variables required for beamforming design, and recover the beamforming vectors through a hybrid training strategy for sum-rate maximization. Furthermore, to address the impact of channel estimation and prediction errors, we propose a neural-network-based robust beamforming method, which maximizes the target minimum-user-rate quantile under an outage probability constraint. In this way, the proposed framework not only mitigates the performance degradation caused by outdated CSI, but also further extends the design to imperfect-CSI scenarios by accounting for both channel estimation errors and the inevitable prediction errors. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method improves channel prediction accuracy, downlink sum-rate performance, and robust minimum-rate guarantees compared with state-of-the-art benchmark schemes.

item.title: Multi-Beamforming Enhanced Multi-Layer Aerial Corridor Coverage for Urban Air Mobility
item.description: Thank you for pointing out this issue. Urban Air Mobility (UAM) relies on dynamic digital air corridors that demand agile and scalable coverage from Low-Altitude Wireless Access Networks (LAWN). While large-scale phased arrays offer the necessary beamforming flexibility, their deployment in multi-layer UAM corridors is hindered by dual manifestations of distortion: i) spatial distortion, arising from the nonlinear mapping between planar corridor geometry and the array spherical angle domain; ii) signal distortion, induced by power amplifier nonlinearities under the high transmit power required for ground-to-air links. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multi-beam coverage model for multi-layer aerial corridors using a uniform planar array. We address the difficulty in dividing multiple beams caused by the nonlinear distortion of spherical angle domain projection. We propose a multi-beamforming scheme that considers the impact of device nonlinear distortion, aiming to maximize the average transmission rate of the system. We propose a virtual subarray reuse scheme. By adjusting the positions of the virtual subarray centers within the physical array, we achieve a more uniform power distribution across the physical array elements, thereby mitigating the effects of device nonlinear distortion. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed virtual subarray scheme can enhance the system throughput by up to 21.6% without increasing the number of array elements.

item.title: Secure and Resilient Cluster Head Election for UAV-Assisted IoV: A Synergistic Approach With Trust Fusion and Dynamic Fitness
item.description: In the UAV-assisted Internet of Vehicles (IoV), UAVs act as relays to enlarge the network coverage. The UAV swarms are divided into different clusters and a cluster head is elected in each cluster to efficiently manage the networks. Before making cluster head election, a node trust evaluation is necessary for securing the election process. To make cluster head election and node trust evaluation simultaneous, this paper proposes an adaptive trust and fluctuation-aware (ATFA) cluster head election mechanism for UAV-assisted IoV. The ATFA mechanism mainly consists of three parts: trust evaluation, fitness evaluation, and cluster head election. In the trust evaluation, we introduce the trust decision index (TDI) to adaptively integrate historical trust and observed trust. In the fitness evaluation, we adopt a fluctuation-aware final scoring mechanism to construct a resource adaptability model based on real-time node degree, centrality, and residual energy. In the cluster head election, both trust score and resource fitness score are considered to effectively select leaders. Experimental results show that ATFA achieves an election accuracy of 97.91%. It reduces the total network communication energy by about two orders of magnitude and reduces the time complexity per election round from quadratic to linear. In addition, ATFA shows clear advantages in robustness and scalability.

item.title: Maximizing the Secrecy Energy Efficiency of Artificial Noise-Assisted Full-Duplex Cooperative NOMA Network With Non-Colluding Eavesdroppers: A Deep Learning Based Approach
item.description: This paper explores the secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) performance of artificial noise (AN)-aided full-duplex cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access (FD-CNOMA) network considering the impact of several non-colluding eavesdroppers. Initially, we focus on determining the optimal power allocation for the downlink users at the BS (BS) as well as the jointly optimal PAC at both the BS and the relay, with the objective of maximizing the SEE. The Dinkelbach-based iterative algorithm is applied to find both the optimal PA and the jointly optimal PA. In-depth numerical studies reveal that the proposed methodologies lead to very high improvement of both SEE as well as the secrecy sum rate (SSR) of the network, compared to random PA and equal PA strategies. To address the computational complexity inherent in iterative optimization algorithm, we develop low-complexity, data-driven inference frameworks that leverage deep neural networks (DNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed models are trained using the optimal solutions obtained from the Dinkelbach iterative algorithm and subsequently employed to infer the optimal PA, jointly optimal PA, and the corresponding SEE. The findings indicate that the suggested learning-based frameworks decrease the inference latency by almost 99% in comparison to the Dinkelbach iterative method. Furthermore, the predicted SEE, optimal PA, and jointly optimal PA are in close alignment with those derived from the optimization-based approach, rendering the proposed frameworks appealing for low-latency and real-time wireless applications.

item.title: Power State Management of Bus-Mounted Edge Servers Toward Elastic Computation Offloading: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
item.description: In vehicular networks, user devices can offload their computation tasks to edge servers placed at fixed-site locations, e.g., RoadSide Units (RSUs) and base stations. However, these fixed-site servers require land resources and construction space, and their static computation capacity often fails to support dynamic user demands, e.g., power waste during leisure time and capacity deficit during rush hours. In this paper, we study the power management of public bus-mounted edge servers to tackle such spatiotemporal dynamics. We first model the dynamic power state management problem of bus-mounted edge servers as a multi-objective optimization problem, which aims at minimizing the energy consumption and task processing delay through turning on/off the bus-mounted servers when necessary. To solve it, we design DS-D3QN, a Dynamic Sleep management algorithm based on Dueling Double Deep Q-Learning Networks, through which the edge computing service on a bus is turned on in the areas experiencing a surge demand, and switched off to save energy when the surrounding demand is low. Trace-driven experiments show that our DS-D3QN algorithm demonstrates a better overall performance in terms of energy consumption and task processing delay than the existing popular algorithms.

item.title: Lightweight and Distributed Dynamic Data-Sharing Scheme With Privacy Preservation for VANETs
item.description: Vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs) are pivotal in advancing intelligent driving and enhancing vehicular services. However, they introduce significant risks of data privacy breaches. Although numerous data sharing mechanisms have been proposed, they often suffer from issues such as excessive central authority power, collusion among authorities leading to key leakage, and vulnerabilities to message linking attacks that can facilitate deliberate traffic incidents. Additionally, malicious cloud entities may cause data sharing failures through improper decryption, and the substantial computational overhead is ill-suited for resource-constrained vehicles. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight data sharing scheme based on decentralized ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption scheme tailored for VANETs. Our approach leverages Type-III asymmetric groups to centralize the majority of user computations within a more compact group structure. By utilizing an edge computing framework, we outsource computation-intensive pairing operations to the cloud in a verifiable manner, ensuring that the complexity of access policies does not linearly impact pairing computations. Furthermore, we implement ring signatures to facilitate anonymous communication between vehicles and employ a garbled bloom filter to obscure access policies. A consortium blockchain is deployed to manage multiple attribute authority nodes, which utilize the practical byzantine fault tolerance (PBFT) consensus mechanism for secure revocation processes, thereby preventing malicious or erroneous revocations. Comprehensive security assessments and performance evaluations validate the efficiency and robustness of our scheme within the VANETs environment.

item.title: Lightweight QoS-Aware Routing for Large-Scale LEO Satellite Networks via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, with their potential for global coverage, low latency, and massive connectivity, are emerging as a pivotal component in 6G communications. As an increasing number of communication services rely on satellite transmission, there is an urgent need to design a lightweight Quality of Service (QoS)-aware routing strategy for large-scale LEO satellite networks. However, existing routing schemes struggle to simultaneously satisfy the critical requirements for stringent QoS, lightweight operation, and robust scalability in large-scale LEO constellations with highly dynamic topology. To meet these critical requirements, this paper proposes a Hierarchical QoS-aware Geometric Segment Routing (HQGSR) algorithm. HQGSR divides the network into multiple regions, enabling more lightweight optimization. Specifically, we first establish a region-level QoS model and formulate the corresponding optimization problem. Building upon this, we introduce a Prioritized Deep Reinforcement Learning for Macropath (PDRLMa) algorithm to compute a QoS-aware region-level skeleton path. Furthermore, we design a Local Probabilistic Forwarding for Micropath (LPFMi) algorithm to achieve low-overhead path selection. The experimental results demonstrate that HQGSR provides a lightweight and scalable intelligent routing solution and achieves excellent performance in terms of communication delay, energy consumption, and robustness.

item.title: RIS-Assisted Physical Layer Security: Artificial Noise-Driven Optimization and Measurements
item.description: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has emerged as a key enabler for providing signal coverage, energy efficiency, reliable communication, and physical layer security (PLS) in next-generation wireless communication networks. This paper investigates an artificial noise (AN)-driven RIS-assisted secure communication system. The RIS is partitioned into two segments, where the first segment is configured to direct the communication signal (CS) toward the legitimate user (Bob), and the other one is configured to steer the AN toward the eavesdropper (Eve). To this end, iterative and discrete Fourier transform-based algorithms are developed for practical RIS phase shift optimization. The power allocation between the CS and the AN signals is optimized in such a way that the secrecy capacity (SC) is maximized while limiting Eve's channel capacity. The proposed PLS framework is evaluated through both simulations and software defined radio based testbed experiments. The results demonstrate promising improvements in the SC, highlighting the potential of AN-driven RIS-assisted PLS for practical deployments.

item.title: Sensing-Assisted Beam Tracking in Cell-Free ISAC
item.description: In this paper, we investigate cell-free integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems and propose a sensing-assisted beam tracking scheme based on multiple access point (AP) cooperation. Leveraging the Bayesian filtering framework, the proposed scheme integrates prior state transitions with posterior filtering to achieve optimal tracking. Since the echoes received at each AP may contain contributions from multiple user terminals (UTs), we apply point-wise division and the two-dimensional Fourier transform to map these echoes into the delay-Doppler domain, thereby enabling distinguishing signals from different UTs. To further reduce computational complexity, we discard low-power components and focus on dominant parts by exploiting the sparsity of UT signals in the delay-Doppler domain. Moreover, the nonlinearity of state transition and observation models renders the direct computation of prior and posterior probability density functions intractable. To address this challenge, we employ particle filtering to provide a Monte Carlo approximation of the Bayesian filtering. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

item.title: Efficient Constant Envelope Precoding for Massive MU-MIMO With 1-Bit DAC
item.description: Massive multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) is a cornerstone of 5G technology, offering significant gains in data rate and network capacity.However, its deployment is challenged by the high energy consumption and hardware costs of large antenna arrays at base stations. The use of 1-bit constant envelope (CE) precoding has emerged as an effective solution to reduce both power consumption and hardware complexity. Designing 1-bit CE precoding involves a non-convex combinatorial optimization problem with tightly coupled variables, which is computationally challenging. This paper proposes a novel algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and the heavy-ball (HB) method to efficiently solve this problem. Our approach provides an exact solution with notably lower computational complexity. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing schemes, achieving improved bit error rate (BER) and faster convergence.

item.title: Thickness-Dependent Performance of Undoped Polycrystalline CdSeTe-Only Solar Cells: n-type Behavior and Hole Diffusion Length From Modeling
item.description: Selenium has improved carrier lifetime and luminescence in CdSexTe1-x/cadmium telluride (CdTe) bi-layer absorbers. Without a CdTe layer, uniform bandgap, without any intentional doping (undoped), CdSeTe-only (or CST-only) absorbers exhibited higher external radiative efficiency and carrier lifetimes compared to bi-layer absorbers. However, this did not translate into device performance. This has been attributed to poor hole mobility in the undoped CdSeTe-only absorber due to the presence of hole traps. In this study, we demonstrate that the limited device performance stems from the n-type nature of undoped CdSeTe-only absorber within p-type device architecture. A significant improvement in power conversion efficiency from <5% to 13.4% was achieved by reducing the absorber thickness to less than one micron, one of the highest reported for this technology. Poor device performance in undoped thicker absorbers is attributed to limited hole (minority carrier) diffusion. Through solar cell capacitance simulator (SCAPS) modeling, hole diffusion length in these absorbers, with electron concentration of 3 × 1015 cm−3 (extracted from C–V measurement), was estimated to be in the range of 0.5–0.9 μm.

item.title: Alkali Metal Halide Synergistic Regulation on Bulk and Interfacial Defects in Quantum Dot/Perovskite Hybrid Nanorod Array Solar Cells
item.description: The core-shell nanorod architectures provide an ideal platform for integrating the near-infrared response of semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) with perovskites, owing to their superior light harvesting capability and directed charge transport characteristics. However, the heterogeneous interfaces within such hybrid systems inevitably introduce detrimental defects that exacerbate carrier recombination losses. Herein, we report a synergistic passivation strategy employing potassium iodide (KI) to simultaneously modulate the bulk crystallization quality of MAPbI3 and the interfacial defect states of lead sulfide QDs. The influence of KI concentration ([K+] / ([MA+] + [K+]) = 0.05–0.20) on the structural, optical, photovoltaic, and carrier dynamic properties of the hybrid nanorod arrays was systematically investigated. The incorporation of KI yields dual positive effects: on the one hand, it optimizes the crystallization kinetics of the perovskite, promoting enlarged grain size (increasing from 209 to 235 nm in diameter) and reduced Urbach energy (from 0.0907 to 0.0825 eV), thereby effectively suppressing nonradiative recombination in both the bulk and at the interfaces. On the other hand, K+ ions accumulate at interfaces to neutralize charge accumulation, while I− ions fill iodine vacancies and passivate undercoordinated Pb2+ sites, leading to significantly enhanced interfacial charge extraction efficiency with the charge transfer resistance Rct decreasing from 314.9 to 54.35 Ω. Consequently, at [K+] / ([MA+] + [K+]) = 0.20, the optimized device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 10.24% with a Voc of 0.837 V and a Jsc of 19.42 mA/cm2, representing a substantial improvement over control devices without KI. This work demonstrates an effective approach for the synergistic regulation of bulk and interfacial defects via alkali metal halides, offering new insights for the design of high-efficiency near-infrared-responsive perovskite–quantum dot hybrid photovoltaic devices.

item.title: Qualification of Photovoltaic Micromodules via Time-Domain Reflectometry Signature Testing for Energy-Harvesting Applications: A Novel Methodology
item.description: Photovoltaic micromodules employed in energy-harvesting and Internet of Things applications remain outside conventional qualification standards, which are primarily defined for full-size modules above 5 Wp. This regulatory gap creates reliability challenges for low-power autonomous systems operating under strict size and maintenance constraints. Although time-domain techniques, such as time-domain reflectometry (TDR) and spread-spectrum TDR, have been widely applied for fault detection in PV arrays, they have not been established as device-level qualification methodologies. This work proposes a qualification framework for crystalline silicon PV micromodules based on high-resolution TDR electronic signature masks. The reflected parameter $S_{11}$ is acquired using a vector network analyzer under dark conditions and converted to nanosecond-resolution time-domain signatures via standardized frequency-to-time reconstruction. From a statistically characterized healthy population, pass/fail TDR acceptance masks are derived. Accelerated reliability tests (salt mist, damp heat, and thermal cycling) were conducted to induce representative degradation mechanisms. A significant portion of degraded samples exhibited perceptible deviations from the defined masks, while others remained within acceptance limits depending on the nature and severity of the degradation mechanism. The proposed methodology establishes a scalable, nondestructive and statistically grounded qualification tool tailored to PV micromodules for IoT energy-harvesting applications.

item.title: Different Damp-Heat-Induced Series Resistance Degradation Behaviors in Fielded Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Modules Due to Difference in Bill of Materials
item.description: This case study investigates mono-crystalline silicon modules from underperforming portions of a utility-scale photovoltaic power plant. Field-collected I-V curves and electroluminescence imaging suggested that increased series resistance was a primary factor driving module degradation. Selected modules were removed from the field for further analysis, including incremental damp heat accelerated testing, which confirmed a progression in series resistance degradation. Two distinct cell degradation behaviors became apparent during the investigation. Cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy (with elemental analysis) and scanning spreading resistance microscopy identified key differences between the two degradation mechanisms, primarily grid finger width and contact resistance. Additionally, the study highlights the reliability implications of retest requirements in International Electrotechnical Commission 61215 for material changes and how they may have mitigated the degradation observed at this site.

item.title: From Probabilistic Power Baselines to Closed-Loop PV Cleaning: Residual-Based Soiling Quantification and Rolling-Horizon Optimization
item.description: Surface soiling on photovoltaic (PV) modules exhibits pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity and remains difficult to quantify online. Consequently, cleaning decisions often rely on empirical thresholds, making it challenging to consistently balance power-generation gains against maintenance costs under uncertain weather disturbances. To address these issues, this article proposes a closed-loop “prediction-estimation-decision” framework that reformulates PV cleaning as a residual-state feedback decision problem. Unlike cleaning-scheduling methods that rely on prescribed or externally measured soiling states, the proposed framework constructs a probabilistic clean-power baseline and infers the soiling-induced loss online from the residual between the baseline and the measured power. The inferred soiling-loss state is then used to update rolling-horizon cleaning decisions under weather feasibility, economic return, and operating constraints. Specifically, a multivariate data-fusion Transformer (MFT) probabilistic forecasting model is developed using meteorological variables, historical power data, and temporal encodings to generate the clean-power baseline with uncertainty bounds. The residual between this baseline and the measured output is converted into an online estimate of the soiling-loss rate, providing a quantitative basis for cleaning decisions without dedicated soiling sensors. A multilayer rolling-horizon optimization (RHO) strategy is further designed to coordinate cleaning triggering and cleaning intensity while using prediction intervals to mitigate spurious triggering during abrupt weather changes. Experimental results show that the MFT model achieves RMSE, MAE, and nRMSE values of 0.2886, 0.1871, and 0.0265, respectively. The proposed strategy improves net profit by 87.0% compared with fixed-threshold methods, and ablation studies confirm the roles of the feasibility, economic, and execution-feedback layers in maintaining stable closed-loop operation. These results indicate that residual-based soiling quantification can provide a decision-oriented link between probabilistic PV forecasting and adaptive cleaning control.

item.title: Field Performance Analysis of Bifacial Photovoltaic Modules Using Ground Reflection Spectra and View Factor Models
item.description: The field performance of bifacial photovoltaic (PV) modules is influenced by both the ground reflection spectrum and the irradiance distribution on the backside surface. The reflection spectrum is dependent on various factors, including air mass and ground surface type, which complicates its evaluation. In this article, a simplified yet accurate reflection spectrum model based on readily available meteorological parameters is proposed and introduced to calculate the reflected solar spectrum for engineering applications. The impact of the reflection spectrum on the performance of bifacial modules is analyzed and quantified using the spectrum mismatch factor, which measures the degree of deviation between the actual and standard spectra. In addition, a calculation method for the output power of the module is introduced, incorporating the view factor model for backside irradiance. Experimental designs conducted on grassland, soil, and concrete demonstrate the accuracy and applicability of both the reflection spectrum model and the power calculation method. The results indicate that in all three scenarios, the reflection model demonstrates high accuracy, with an average error within 10%. After correction with the spectral mismatch factor, the average accuracy of total power prediction for bifacial modules in three scenarios increased from 91.81% to 96.41%; compared with the traditional fixed broadband reflectance method, the relative errors of power prediction in the three scenarios were reduced from 14.75%, 14.68%, and 5.21% to 2.67%, 1.90%, and 1.44%, significantly improving prediction accuracy and enhancing the fault diagnosis capability in intelligent operation and maintenance of PV systems.

item.title: A Fully Passive Second-Order Charge-Domain Noise-Shaping Digital Bang--Bang PLL With Adaptive DCO Gain Controller
item.description: Quantization noise (QN) is recognized as a primary factor limiting the in-band phase-noise and jitter performance of digital bang–bang phase-locked loops (BBPLLs), while the nonlinear loop gain introduced by the binary phase detector further degrades jitter performance. In order to address these issues, a fully passive second-order noise-shaping BBPLL (NS-BBPLL) with an adaptive digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) gain controller is presented in this article. A fully passive noise-shaping phase detector (NSPD) is employed, by which the phase difference is processed in the charge domain, and second-order shaping of the phase-detector QN is achieved, thereby effectively suppressing its in-band contribution. As a result, a measured 6-dB in-band phase-noise improvement is achieved through the combined reduction of the detector quantization- and thermal-noise (TN) contributions, with the larger reduction observed in the QN term. In addition, an adaptive DCO gain controller based on a symbolic least-mean-squares (LMSs) algorithm is introduced to automatically optimize the loop bandwidth and improve the overall jitter performance. The proposed integer- $N$ NS-BBPLL is fabricated in a 65-nm process, with a core area of 0.12 mm2. The core circuit’s power consumption is 2.50 mW at an output frequency of 4.8 GHz. Jitter of 305 fsrms is achieved, and the reference spur is measured at −59 dBc, resulting in a figure of merit (FoM) of −246.3 dB.

item.title: LUT-DiT: A LUT-Based Diffusion Transformer Accelerator for Scalable LUT Inference
item.description: Large-scale diffusion transformers (DiTs) (e.g., FLUX.1) deliver strong generation quality but face severe memory and latency bottlenecks. Although lookup table (LUT)-based inference eliminates expensive multiplications, conventional LUT schemes that precompute all weight-activation combinations suffer from prohibitive table growth, resulting in 178.81 GB of precomputed tables for FLUX.1 under W4A4 quantization. To address this problem, this article proposes LUT-DiT, a LUT-based DiT accelerator for scalable LUT inference. First, we employ outlier-aware product quantization (PQ) to map weights into a compact codebook domain, thereby shifting precomputation from the full weight domain to the codebook domain. Second, we introduce a two-level lookup mechanism that reformulates full weight-activation precomputation as index-to-codebook mapping followed by codebook-activation lookup, reducing memory complexity from $O(N_{\text {weight}}{\,}\times {\,}2^{b_{\text {act}}})$ to $O(N_{\text {codebook}}{\,}\times {\,}2^{b_{\text {act}}})$ . Third, we design a pipelined datapath with input-channel (IC) sharing and symmetry-based compression, reducing the active on-chip working set of precomputed tables to 2.75 KB. This compact working set is efficiently managed by a three-level on-chip storage hierarchy. Experimental results on FLUX.1 show that LUT-DiT reduces the global off-chip storage required by precomputed tables from 178.81 to 5.124 GB, achieving a $34.9\times $ reduction, while delivering $3.15\times $ higher throughput (steps/s) and $6.76\times $ higher energy efficiency than an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. Compared with the gains reported by Diff-DiT over its GPU baseline, the corresponding ratios of reported gains are $2.26\times $ and $1.21\times $ for throughput and energy efficiency, respectively.

item.title: A 9.75-Gb/s Matrix-Assisted Anchor-Decoding TPC Decoder for NAND Flash Memories
item.description: With the increasing storage demand driven by artificial intelligence and other data-intensive applications, nand flash memories require error-correction code (ECC) solutions that provide sufficient correction capability while maintaining low power consumption. Although low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoders are widely used in modern nand flash controllers, their soft-decision decoding process usually introduces high implementation complexity and power overhead. Turbo product codes (TPCs), which rely on iterative hard-decision decoding (iHDD), offer a low-complexity alternative. In this work, a matrix-assisted anchor-decoding (MA-AD) TPC decoder architecture is proposed. The proposed design employs an error matrix, conflict registers, and a rollback handling unit to realize conflict detection and rollback operations. By reorganizing the dynamic and irregular anchor-decoding procedure into a static matrix-assisted decoding flow, the proposed architecture becomes more suitable for hardware implementation. Compared with the conventional extended Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (eBCH)-based TPC decoder, the proposed MA-AD TPC decoder improves the correction capability in the waterfall region by 0.25 dB with a limited reduction in throughput. Implementation results show that the proposed decoder achieves an area of 0.49 mm2, a throughput of 9.75 Gb/s, and an energy efficiency of 6.5 pJ/bit.

item.title: An NRZ/PAM-4 Dual-Mode Transmitter Using Tx-Interleaving Technique for Low-Power DRAM Interfaces
item.description: This article proposes a nonreturn-to-zero (NRZ)/PAM-4 dual-mode transmitter for low-power double data rate (LPDDR) memory interfaces that employs a transmitter-interleaving (TI) technique to enhance power efficiency while maintaining high-speed signaling capability. Instead of separate data and clock paths in the conventional dual-mode transmitters, the proposed architecture inserts clock-controlled NMOS switches into the low-voltage swing-terminated logic (LVSTL) output driver structure, thereby merging the serialization path with the driver stage. This structural integration eliminates the need for a dedicated high-speed serializer and reduces switching activity in the driver block. A prior TI driver-based transmitter requires a clock bootstrapping circuit and typically does not support ZQ calibration, resulting in impedance mismatch. In contrast, this work removes the bootstrapping circuit and adopts a dual-mode ZQ calibration scheme that maintains constant output impedance across both NRZ and PAM-4 modes. A prototype chip is fabricated in a 1-poly 10-metal (1P10LM) 28-nm CMOS process. Measured results demonstrate that the proposed transmitter consumes 10.82 mW while transmitting 11-Gb/s PAM-4 data, achieving an energy efficiency of 0.98-pJ/b, confirming that the proposed structure is highly suitable for LPDDR.

item.title: Leak-CIM: A PVT-Robust and Energy-Efficient SRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro Exploiting Transistor Leakage
item.description: The binarized neural networks (BNNs) significantly reduce arithmetic and storage costs for edge inference, but repeated bitwise accumulation and memory access still limit system energy efficiency. This article presents leak-computing-in-memory (CIM), a $256\times 64$ static random access memory (SRAM)-based voltage-mode CIM macro that exploits the subthreshold leakage of off-state transistors as ultrahigh-impedance pseudo-resistors for low-energy analog accumulation. Unlike charge-sharing CIMs, the proposed scheme maintains a wide read-bitline (RBL) dynamic range while strongly suppressing the shoot-through current that typically limits voltage-mode operation. To compensate for the process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensitivity of leakage-based pull-up and pull-down paths, the leak-CIM employs a postfabrication N-well bias calibration scheme that restores their resistance balance. The postlayout simulations show that the calibrated macro maintains a normalized mean-squared error below $1.12\times 10^{-2}$ across 40 global PVT conditions. Fabricated in a 22-nm bulk-CMOS process, the macro achieves up to 1799 TOPS/W and 31.67 TOPS/mm2 across measured operating points. When the measured ADC characteristics are incorporated into a BNN inference model, leak-CIM attains 98.15% accuracy on MNIST and 86.04% on CIFAR-10.

item.title: A 28-nm Floating-Point SRAM-CIM Macro With In-Array Shifting for Exponent Normalization and Mantissa Alignment Based on Exponent Midrange
item.description: Floating-point computing-in-memory (FP-CIM) macros typically suffer from prohibitive area and power overheads due to the complexity of alignment logic. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel FP-CIM macro that integrates two key in-memory operations: shifting-in-memory exponent normalization (SIMENP) and shifting-in-memory mantissa alignment (SIMMAP). SIMENP enables in-array exponent shifting using the proposed 9T bitcell, thereby eliminating redundant processing latency. For mantissa alignment, a midrange-based subtraction-shifting scheme is implemented using the proposed 10T bitcell, which obviates the need for dedicated shift registers while halving the clock cycles required for data shifting. The proposed macro is designed and simulated in a 28-nm CMOS process with a 36-kB capacity. Simulation results demonstrate an energy efficiency of 11.63 TFLOPS/W at 150 MHz under a 0.55 V supply. Compared to state-of-the-art subtractor-based FP-CIM architectures and D flip-flop (DFF) combined schemes, the proposed design reduces the shifting-logic area by 45.7%, while also reducing the number of cycles required for mantissa alignment by 50%.

item.title: Instruction-Driven Dynamically Reconfigurable Lockstep Architecture for Runtime Reliability
item.description: Advanced process scaling has introduced significant reliability challenges where microprocessors exhibit highly dynamic sensitivity to transient faults across varying operating environments and application phases. Conventional static lockstep architectures impose rigid redundancy levels, leading to either permanent resource wastage or an inflexible reliability boundary. This article presents an instruction-driven dynamically reconfigurable lockstep architecture that provides a continuum of capabilities for requirement-defined redundancy. Leveraging custom RISC-V instruction set architecture (ISA) extensions, software modulates hardware resources across six operational modes, ranging from high-performance symmetric independent execution to high-reliability triple-core lockstep (TCLS). This reconfiguration is managed by a lockstep controller and an access switching unit (ASU) matrix, achieving mode transitions within a deterministic window of 3–10 cycles. Implemented on 28-nm CMOS, the triple-core CV32E40P cluster achieves 617 MHz. Compared to a standalone baseline core, the architecture occupies $3.18\times $ area and consumes $2.64\times $ power, with a marginal frequency penalty of 4.94%. Fault injection campaigns confirm a bounded recovery latency of less than 115 cycles across all redundancy modes. This framework enables software-defined alignment of hardware reliability with runtime requirements.

item.title: DSRVC-DP: A High-Performance Domain-Specific Controller With Memoized CORDIC Extension of RISC-V for Digital Power Applications
item.description: Digital power control applications impose stringent real-time computational demands, particularly for trigonometric operations in closed-loop systems. To address this challenge, we propose a domain-specific RISC-V controller for digital power (DSRVC-DP), a customized controller based on the tinyriscv open-source processor. The design extends the RISC-V instruction set with hardware-accelerated trigonometric operations via a memoized CORDIC unit, which exploits data reuse to eliminate redundant iterations. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements over DSP and ARM controllers. Single-angle evaluation and trigonometric-table generation are significantly accelerated, and the interrupt service routine (ISR) execution time in closed-loop control is reduced by 48% and 27% in inverter control, and by 36% and 11% in the phase-locked-loop (PLL) applications, respectively. These results confirm DSRVC-DP’s effectiveness in enhancing real-time performance for digital power control.

item.title: TREA: Low-Precision Time-Multiplexed, Resource-Efficient Edge Accelerator for Object Detection and Classification
item.description: This work presents TREA, a low-precision, time-multiplexed, and resource-efficient edge-AI accelerator for object detection and classification, targeting the stringent area-power-latency constraints of edge vision platforms. The proposed architecture integrates a dual-precision (4-/8-bit) quantized SIMD MAC (DQ-MAC) unit based on most-significant-digit-first (MSDF) shift-and-add computation with runtime bit truncation, eliminating conventional multiplier overhead and reducing the accumulator bit width. The DQ-multiply-accumulate (MAC) supports $4\times $ F $\times $ P4 or $1\times $ F $\times $ P8 operations per cycle, achieving up to $4\times $ throughput improvement without hardware duplication. A structured hardware-aware reductive pruning (SHARP) strategy is co-designed with the single instruction multiple data (SIMD) datapath, enabling near 50% structured sparsity while maintaining full MAC utilization. This allows a $3 \times 3$ convolution kernel to be computed in 1 cycle in F $\times $ P4 mode, compared to 9 cycles in F $\times $ P8, and a $5 \times 5$ kernel in 3 cycles, versus 25 cycles, yielding up to a $9\times $ latency reduction at the kernel level. The accelerator further incorporates a shared reconfigurable quantise-enabled CORDIC-based nonlinear activation function (RQ-NAF) core with a nine-stage pipeline, supporting Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at one output per cycle after pipeline fill, while enabling (N-1) hardware reuse through time-multiplexing. The complete TREA architecture employs a 1-D array of 128 SIMD DQ-MAC units with layerwise hardware reuse, significantly reducing area and control complexity.
